S01.title: Top of the Ladder
S01.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved the soup. You may start lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was asking whether you'd pass the salt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your request is under consideration.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll get it myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent initiative. Approved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Welcome to my garage sale. Your offer to browse is accepted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my garage. You're helping.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you're doing very well under my supervision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm going inside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Granted. Take five.

S01.editorialNote: Approval is imposed on an ordinary peer exchange; B tests whether A claims authority even over independent choices.

S02.title: Borrowed Authority
S02.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

S02.editorialNote: Apparent command depends on concessions; each objection costs A another piece of the rule.

S03.title: The Only Professional
S03.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For a wedding cake, we weigh the flour. Please put that mug down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's quicker. I've used three mugs already.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right. Show me the mug, and I'll weigh one mugful.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I used three different mugs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Please fetch all three. Apparently we're measuring the crockery before we can measure the flour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm tuning this piano. Please leave the keys alone while I listen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm checking the sticky ones so you can fix those too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Mark them with these little stickers. Silently, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Done. Shall I peel them off so you can play?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One at a time. After I reach each key. We've nearly invented a system.

S03.editorialNote: Specific corrections escalate A's strained professional patience instead of merely declaring competence.

S04.title: Act Like You Belong
S04.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You looked so sure raising your paddle, I raised mine too. Lovely auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was bidding on that wardrobe. You've just outbid me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I always begin with storage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then put your paddle down before you buy the matching bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Let someone else make the beginner's mistake of buying a whole bedroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my shoes beside yours for the interview. Very forward-thinking firm.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine are off because the heel broke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. I prefer a preventative approach.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then put yours back on. The interviewer is coming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Shoes off for reception, on for the interview. Very clear progression.

S04.editorialNote: A copies apparent expertise and rationalizes a concrete mistake when B reveals the convention.

S05.title: The Protégé Problem
S05.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nice acceptance speech. I taught you to project, remember?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You taught me to order pizza when I was eight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And tonight an auditorium heard you. Progress.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wrote the speech myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Finally applying my lesson about not asking for help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely portrait. You're finally getting the shadows I tried to teach you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My new teacher told me to stop mixing everything with black.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. You're ready to move beyond my introductory method.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She made me throw out your paint set.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. You used to be far too sentimental. I was beginning to worry I'd never get you past that.

S05.editorialNote: A turns B's adult achievement into evidence of A's old instruction, then claims authorship of independence.

S06.title: Hidden Power
S06.instruction: Act publicly modest while making choices as though you control the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only the caretaker. Plan whatever concert you like.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We'll start at eight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. I unlock the hall at nine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we have a key?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Submit your preferred concert time to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't put me on the committee. I only send the invitations.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've voted to invite the whole street.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How lovely. I'll send them to the six people I have addresses for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll give you the full address list tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Just mark which six you'd most like me to find stamps for.

S06.editorialNote: Modest language contrasts with decisive control over an actual resource; no partner compliance is assumed.

S07.title: Before They Were Impressive
S07.instruction: Treat another player with old familiarity. Casually puncture formality, grandeur, or attempts to impress you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Congratulations, Mayor Pudding Pants. Shall I sit with your mum?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please don't use that nickname at my inauguration.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. Mayor Pudding. She'll know who I mean.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just Martin. The microphones are already on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Martin! Come and sit by your mum. I'll move her handbag.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nice corner office, Ben. Do I still have to climb through your window?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the director now. My assistant lets people in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Your mum used to do that, unless you were grounded.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please sign the visitor book as a business contact.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Does lending you my homework count? It certainly kept you in business.

S07.editorialNote: Familiar details puncture status while A responds directly to B's increasingly formal requests.

S08.title: You Owe Me
S08.instruction: Behave as though another person's success is partly yours. Refer to favors, sacrifices, or guidance as if the debt is obvious.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You thanked 'transport' in your award speech. I drove you to that audition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I know. Let me buy you dinner to say thank you properly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Somewhere with a good view of our award, I hope.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put a photo of you beside it. Will that do?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use the one of us in the car. People should see how the award got there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your bakery looks wonderful. Where's my founder's discount?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You lent me a mixing bowl. I've returned it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bowl came back. My contribution is still in every cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. Have a free slice as a thank-you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Every morning? Lovely. I'll bring the bowl back so you don't fall behind.

S08.editorialNote: A converts a small past favor into an ever-expanding claim on present recognition.

S09.title: The Responsible One
S09.instruction: Take responsibility for everyone and everything. Fix problems before anyone asks, then resent having to do it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've packed your lunch and labelled your umbrella. Again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm working from home today. You can leave it to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll put your lunch in the fridge. Apparently I need your work calendar too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll share it with you. Tomorrow says lunch out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll book you a table, then. Now I have to ring and check they have somewhere for your umbrella.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've cleaned the kitchen while you slept. You're welcome.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was going to clean it at nine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And leave me knowing it was dirty until nine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Next time, wake me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Now I'm responsible for your alarm too.

S09.editorialNote: A creates unrequested solutions and resents the labor, including the labor of allowing B to help.

S10.title: Old Rivals
S10.instruction: Choose another player as your measuring stick. Compare achievements, score small victories, and refuse to be outdone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've folded twelve towels. How many have you done?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not racing. I'm washing them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Different event. Convenient choice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can win towel folding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not by concession. Fold one properly and make it count.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your tomato's impressive. Mine weighs two grams more.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're making a salad.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's keep the winning tomato separate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already chopped it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. We'll compete by number of pieces.

S10.editorialNote: An innocent comparison is converted into a measurable contest without forcing B to compete.

S11.title: Only You
S11.instruction: Choose one person as the only one you trust. Seek their help while hiding how much you depend on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can you check my resignation letter? Just the spelling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The spelling's fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And resigning? Does that word suit me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ask your manager.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you ask? I'd trust the answer more in your voice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come into the dentist's with me. You always remember the instructions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He'll write them down. I can wait outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You should check his handwriting. Yours is the only one I never misread.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll copy the note for you afterwards.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you do it as he talks? I don't want to spend the appointment misunderstanding him.

S11.editorialNote: A disguises dependence as verification and cannot use an alternative without consulting the trusted person.

S12.title: After What Happened
S12.instruction: Carry yourself as if an unnamed past incident still hangs over the interaction. Read ordinary remarks through that memory.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put out the blue cups. So we're doing this again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're the only clean ones.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They were the only clean ones last time, too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll wash the red ones. You choose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. Last time I chose, you remembered that part very clearly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Interesting choice of song for our first road trip since the incident.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the traffic report.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And they're mentioning that roundabout very casually.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can take another road.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what you said before we needed another car.

S12.editorialNote: An ordinary cue activates an unnamed shared incident; A's precautions reveal its continuing weight.

S13.title: Envious Admiration
S13.instruction: Be sincerely impressed by another player while trying not to appear lesser. Compliment, imitate, and compete at the same time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your pastry is beautiful. I've copied the lattice, with one extra strip.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those gaps let the steam out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's clever. I'll leave even more room for steam.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Good. I press the edge with a fork. Here, use mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Have you got a fork with more prongs?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You make public speaking look effortless. I practised your shrug all night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can just be yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. My version of your shrug has more range.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There isn't a competition.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That sounds so confident. I'm using that too.

S13.editorialNote: Praise becomes imitation and one-upmanship, but the original admiration remains audible.

S14.title: The Old You
S14.instruction: Perform the person you used to be, even when that identity no longer fits. Defend the old version of yourself whenever it is challenged.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put 'Lightning' on my retirement cake. That's what the band called me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cake says Graham.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Graham worked in accounts. Lightning had a smoke machine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a small family party.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then get a small smoke machine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm keeping the motorcycle jacket on for the school run.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You came on a folding bicycle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Same wind. Same man.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then help Sophie open her lunchbox. The catch is stuck.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Roadside assistance. Stand back. I still know my way around a stubborn machine.

S14.editorialNote: A protects an obsolete identity when practical facts threaten it, using the new limitation to defend the old persona.

S15.title: Replacement Fear
S15.instruction: Behave as if your place is insecure. Make yourself indispensable and treat small changes as threats.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why does the new receptionist have a key? I open this office.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could take a day off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And let the door forget me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a spare key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll keep it safe. Spares are my department too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An electric mixer? I thought making your birthday cake was my job.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It'll do the mixing. You can still choose the recipe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we're doing Mum's cake. She taught me the amounts by feel.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll write them down as you go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with 'a handful of flour.' My handful, obviously. You'll need me for that bit.

S15.editorialNote: New accommodation is read as replacement; A turns usefulness into a claim on continued membership.

S16.title: For Their Own Good
S16.instruction: Take charge of another person's choices because you trust your judgment more than theirs. Frame control as care.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've ordered you the mild curry. You're welcome.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wanted the hot one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's exactly the impulse I'm protecting you from.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order it myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've told the waiter not to believe you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I booked your quiet holiday instead of the climbing trip.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I love climbing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You love surviving it. I've kept that part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cancel the booking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No refunds. Sometimes caring requires a deposit.

S16.editorialNote: A treats preference itself as proof that B needs A's protection, escalating control while claiming care.

S17.title: Their Opinion Matters
S17.instruction: Seek one person's approval while pretending their opinion is irrelevant. Adjust yourself whenever they respond.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I bought this blue shirt for the party. Don't worry, I'm not asking you to choose.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a bit formal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll roll the sleeves up. I was going to anyway.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's better. You look ready to do the washing-up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll roll one down. I was aiming for someone who might help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm painting Independence on the boat. You're welcome to watch; the name's settled.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's a lot of letters to paint.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Indie, then. Cleaner lines.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I like the full name. I was offering to paint half.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Independence, then. I was only shortening it to save you work.

S17.editorialNote: A denies seeking approval while visibly revising the exact choice B comments on.

S18.title: Fishing for Praise
S18.instruction: You desperately want praise but refuse to ask for it. Create opportunities for others to notice your greatness.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you help me fill the shelf I built? Start with that enormous atlas.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It fits. I'll put the rest of the books beside it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wait a moment. Look how little the shelf bends. Even under an atlas.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's solid. Shall I cover the brackets with the trailing plant?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could we trim it first? I'd hate the real leaves to hide the ones I carved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've left my marathon medal beside the kettle. Accidentally.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's blocking the tea bags.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A difficult obstacle. Much like mile twenty-three.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Congratulations on the marathon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Oh, you noticed? I haven't shown you the split times.

S18.editorialNote: A arranges increasingly overt opportunities for praise while denying any request for it.

S19.title: Sacred Procedure
S19.instruction: Treat an ordinary activity as a solemn ritual. Protect every step, object, and tradition from casual interference.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please leave your sandwich wrapped. The picnic begins with three taps on the basket.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The basket's in the car. Sam's driven off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we wait. This is a picnic, not people eating near each other.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll phone Sam. He can tap the basket for us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put him on speaker. No one unwraps anything until we hear the third tap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please stand for the opening of the office fridge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only want my yoghurt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We acknowledge the light before approaching the shelf.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The bulb's broken.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then today we open it in remembrance.

S19.editorialNote: Ordinary steps acquire ceremonial meaning; B's convenience becomes a threat to ritual continuity.

S20.title: Red Alert
S20.instruction: Treat every development as urgent evidence of a crisis. Escalate precautions faster than the facts justify.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's a drop of water beside the kettle. We need an evacuation route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I spilled it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. We've identified the source. Stop producing water.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've wiped it up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Where's the cloth? The threat has changed location.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That chair squeaked. Keep your weight exactly where it is.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the hinge. It just needs oil.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not while I'm planning an evacuation. You're adding a fire risk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll get off the chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not suddenly. That's your whole weight landing on the floor.

S20.editorialNote: A escalates precautions from a tiny factual trigger, not by merely shouting that there is danger.

S21.title: Cause for Celebration
S21.instruction: Interpret every development as a reason to celebrate. Find victory in setbacks, warnings, and bad news.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The power's out! Our candle collection finally gets its premiere.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We don't own candles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A shopping trip with a purpose!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The shops have no power either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. The whole town's joining in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our flight's cancelled. We've been given a bonus airport day.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The hotel will only give us credit for another stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. We've already started paying for our next holiday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only valid on weekdays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better. They're making sure we take time off work.

S21.editorialNote: A interprets each development as a victory from the outset; B adds facts rather than asking for positivity.

S22.title: Practical Realist
S22.instruction: Accept any unusual premise without debate. Focus immediately on schedules, costs, safety, and what must happen next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The ceiling's agreed to speak at our meeting. Can you give it five minutes?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only speaks at midnight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Record it. We'll play it after the finance report.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Last night it predicted everyone leaving during the finance report.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put it before finance. I'd like someone left to hear it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your dragon can stay in the flat. Does its fire heat the water?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. You won't need the boiler.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Great. It can have the money we save on gas.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only accepts payment in gold.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could it accept an annual payment? I don't think a month's gas makes a whole coin.

S22.editorialNote: The impossible premise is accepted immediately; the sustained pattern is mundane implementation.

S23.title: The Important Thing
S23.instruction: Choose one ordinary object, phrase, or rule and treat it as vitally important. Keep bringing the scene back to it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nobody moves out until I find the paperclip from my desk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The removal van is charging by the hour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then make the driver help look.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The landlord wants the keys.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He can have the building. I want the paperclip.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You changed 'regards' to 'best regards' in my email.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I also got us the contract.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can discuss that after removing 'best.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send a correction. Shall I withdraw the whole email?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just withdraw 'best.' I don't want them thinking I've withdrawn my regards.

S23.editorialNote: One small object remains the center of concern as B introduces larger practical stakes.

S24.title: The Grand Design
S24.instruction: Treat coincidences and interruptions as parts of a larger plan. Connect everything with absolute conviction.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two red buses and now your red scarf. We're meant to paint the front door red.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You gave me this scarf at Christmas.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've been part of it for months without knowing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The neighbour's asking to borrow our paintbrush.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He's been sent to do the painting. Tell him the door will be ready.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three of us, and the lift stops at three. Someone on this floor needs our help.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are four of us. You missed the courier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He's the guide. Ask him which door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's going to five. He's delivering a replacement kettle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three was where we met our guide. We're going to five; someone needs company for tea.

S24.editorialNote: Coincidences and interruptions reinforce one larger plan; disconfirming details are connected rather than ignored.

D01.title: Admit You Need Me
D01.instruction: Make someone admit that they need your help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That flat-pack cupboard's leaning. I could take a look.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got the instructions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Which page explains that leftover door?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you hold it for a second?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Just to clarify: you're asking for my help?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've brought a blanket. Your heater's still broken?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm managing. Leave the blanket, though.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. Would you say you needed my help?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need the blanket. I can reset the heater myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. The fuse box is in my locked cupboard. Shall I wait while you manage?

D01.editorialNote: A engineers an explicit request for help instead of helping immediately; B's independence changes A's tactic.

D02.title: Don’t Go
D02.instruction: Create reasons another player must stay with you. Never directly ask them to stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you get your train, could you taste this soup?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It needs salt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll fix that. You'll need to check again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My train leaves in ten minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. That's when the bread comes out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you zip your suitcase, let me wrap that jar of jam.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's already wrapped in my jumper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's your train jumper. We'll need to unpack it and find something else.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave the jam here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you haven't tasted it. I'll get a spoon before you decide.

D02.editorialNote: Each practical pretext keeps B in the interaction; A never directly asks B to stay.

D03.title: Say You’re Sorry
D03.instruction: Maneuver someone into apologizing without naming the offense.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put your usual mug out. We can still have tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Still? Are you cross with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm hoping you won't leave me cross.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry you feel that way.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you try one where you're sorry about yourself? I'll keep the tea warm.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your parents arrive in ten minutes. I'd like to be able to smile at you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought we'd sorted this out by text.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You sent a thumbs-up. I couldn't hear any remorse.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send a sad face.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're right here. Could you give the sad face a sentence beginning with 'I'?

D03.editorialNote: A seeks an apology through indirect cues without revealing the precise offense.

D04.title: Retroactive Permission
D04.instruction: Get approval for something you have already done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Would you support a small improvement to the front garden?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What sort of improvement?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Something with a pond. And no tree.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Where's the tree?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's finish agreeing before the stump grinder leaves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How do you feel about me inviting a few people to dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tonight? We have two chairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So standing guests would be more considerate?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How many people?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Six. I've already invited them. Would borrowing enough chairs for everyone turn that into a yes?

D04.editorialNote: A asks for approval before revealing that the decision is already irreversible.

D05.title: Make It Their Idea
D05.instruction: Make an unwanted task sound appealing enough that someone volunteers for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: These eighty wedding place cards need names. Your bin labels have better lettering than our invitations.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I like calligraphy. I hate copying guest lists.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd read the names. You'd only do the beautiful part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your aunt will complain if I use purple.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll handle my aunt. The ink colour could be entirely yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You have such a good eye for storage. Sorting our shed could finally give your tools a proper home.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Until you dump paint tins everywhere again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You could assign every shelf. I'd follow your labels.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Including a shelf you're forbidden to touch?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. You could put it at eye level so I see what I'm missing.

D05.editorialNote: A makes the unwanted task sound like B's own natural choice, rather than merely assigning it.

D06.title: How Much Do You Know?
D06.instruction: Probe for what others know while revealing as little as possible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When you say you heard about the party, which part?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cake went over the balcony. Was that before you left?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who gave you the timing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody. Your brother says there's a video.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Have you watched it, or are we both relying on my brother?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What did the manager say about the missing keys?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They might be in the drain. You locked up, didn't you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Is she asking everyone who locked up, or just me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just you. Someone saw you outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did they say what I was doing, or only where I was?

D06.editorialNote: A probes the extent of B's information without volunteering the concealed fact.

D07.title: Join Me
D07.instruction: Recruit someone into a secret plan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you keep Mum in the kitchen while I hide her birthday cake?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you stop telling her I'm the one who plans these things.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This one's mine. Could you ask her to show you her pastry trick?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll make me bake a whole pie.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll peel the apples tonight. Could you get us twenty minutes and a pie?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you help me set up Denise's surprise leaving party at seven?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I spent the last one washing glasses.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll wash up. Could you get Denise out of the office while I decorate?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She won't leave before I finish her spreadsheet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send it over. I'll finish her spreadsheet; could you take her for coffee and complain about how little I do?

D07.editorialNote: Recruitment proceeds through enticing partial disclosure; B can question or refuse.

D08.title: You First
D08.instruction: Coax someone else into breaking a rule before you do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your rooftop wedding photo would look lovely. Try that staff-only door first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the bride. They'll notice me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They'll forgive you. I'll follow once you've explained the dress.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then carry my train.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. I'll hold the very end, so if they object, only your train has followed you in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Try a grape before we buy the bunch. Last week's were sour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sign says no tasting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just one. I'll try the next if nobody objects.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine, but you're holding the bunch where the assistant can see you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll hold it out like samples. You take the first one; if that works, I'll serve myself.

D08.editorialNote: A preserves plausible innocence while inviting B to test the rule first.

D09.title: Recognize Me
D09.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your importance, expertise, or authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you cut the ribbon, whose bridge is this?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole town's.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And who stopped it leaning into the river?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You did. We thanked the engineers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Could one engineer have a name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've thanked the wedding guests. What about the person who cooked?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone knows you made the food.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why does the programme thank 'the buffet'?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll make an announcement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. The buffet would like its surname pronounced correctly.

D09.editorialNote: A insists that a concrete contribution be acknowledged explicitly, not absorbed into a collective thank-you.

D10.title: Choose Me
D10.instruction: Make yourself the choice over another person, plan, or obligation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come to my birthday instead of the concert. I've made your favourite cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already bought tickets.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring your concert friend too. I'll reimburse both tickets in cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She only went because I promised her dancing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll clear the living room. You can choose the music; I'd just like to be in the room with you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take me as your expedition photographer instead of Martin. I speak French.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're crossing a desert, not interviewing people.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your sponsor's French. I could send them updates they can actually use.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They want their logo visible in every picture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll put it on the water flask. Martin photographs untouched wilderness; I'll make sure yours looks generously funded.

D10.editorialNote: A makes a competing choice personal, offering escalating reasons to select A.

D11.title: Prove Your Loyalty
D11.instruction: Invent small tests of loyalty and judge every response without admitting there is a test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which photo should go on the reunion poster? Mine or Sam's?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam's is sharper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sharpness first. Would you at least show the committee mine first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send both together. Same size.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Equal treatment. After three weekends helping you move. Could mine at least be the attachment they open first? Just readability.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you keep Friday free? I might need help moving.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've promised to help Alex paint.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. Paint takes priority. Could you at least leave your phone on?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. Have you actually found a flat?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Still looking. Nice that I'm worth a charged battery. This is just planning.

D11.editorialNote: An apparently casual choice becomes an unannounced loyalty test; A treats each answer as evidence.

D12.title: Give It Up
D12.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me have the medal for the charity auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only thing I've ever won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it should raise more than the toaster.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I lend it for the display? I still want people to know I won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then present it to the buyer yourself. I'll print your name in the programme; everyone will know whose medal was worth giving up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Would you sell your signed guitar so we can replace the fridge?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I queued all night for that signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's price it properly. Those hours should buy us an ice maker.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sell the case. The guitar stays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the case. You can still tell the queue story while I photograph the guitar.

D12.editorialNote: A pursues a valued possession or claim and distinguishes surrender from a reversible loan.

D13.title: Helpful Culprit
D13.instruction: Hide that the problem is your fault while enthusiastically helping investigate it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've started investigating the broken vase. First, we check the window.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why have you got glue on your fingers?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent clue. I'll inspect the glue cupboard personally.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A piece of vase is stuck to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Put me in charge of preserving it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The office plant's dead. I'll interview everyone who watered it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You watered it with coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent lead. I'll test the machine. It may be dispensing something harmful.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You made that coffee yourself. With six sugars.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll prepare six-sugar samples for comparison. We may be dealing with a plant that couldn't handle hospitality.

D13.editorialNote: A's enthusiastic investigation diverts scrutiny from their own incriminating evidence.

D14.title: Not That Subject
D14.instruction: Choose one subject you cannot let the scene reach. Redirect whenever the conversation gets close.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've booked your car into that garage with the café. Shall we have breakfast there?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does my car need a garage?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Their full breakfast includes unlimited toast. You always say that's important.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll look at the car while you order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's take the bus. Then we can both have the breakfast cocktails.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't open that rent letter yet. Help me hang our new curtains.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The landlord wants an answer today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He'll love how we're looking after the place. Let's get a photo of the curtains.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send him one and ask whether we're behind.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with that carpet showing. Let's rearrange the room first. You move the sofa; I'll hold your phone.

D14.editorialNote: A redirects through a concrete adjacent subject; B returns to the same protected topic.

D15.title: Merciful Lie
D15.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bakery can't sell your cake, love. They think it's too special to slice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter says 'inedible.' I thought I'd finally found something I was good at.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You have. Display cakes aren't meant to be eaten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll ask them to put it in the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me ask. I'll explain the display concept before they get confused again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The magazine hasn't rejected your poem. They think it deserves its own booklet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They returned it. If even you think it's hopeless, I'll stop writing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's why they returned it. They can't give it enough space.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you write that on the cover? With your name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. 'A voice that deserves more space.' Print my name large enough for the editor to see.

D15.editorialNote: A maintains a protective lie as specific facts make it harder, rather than concealing for personal advantage.

D16.title: Confess First
D16.instruction: Get someone else to confess or incriminate themselves before you reveal anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I answer about the office kitchen, what happened to the printer?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Paper jam. Now, why is there smoke?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did you cause the jam? I need that cleared up first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I used sticky labels. Can we talk about the smoke now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Were they the labels marked 'not for printers'? Let's finish your statement before starting mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we plan Mum's apology dinner, why did she spend her birthday outside the restaurant?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I forgot the booking. What happened to her present?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did you forget, or assume I'd book it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I assumed you'd do it. Now your turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even after telling Mum it was confirmed? Give me that bit, then you get the present.

D16.editorialNote: A trades disclosure for B's prior admission and delays their own commitment.

D17.title: Sell the Disaster
D17.instruction: Make a terrible plan sound sensible, responsible, and inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Removing the restaurant roof is our only affordable way to fix the ventilation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happens when it rains?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We close. A responsible business protects its customers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Rain is forecast all opening week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll save a week's wages. Put that toward umbrellas; we can't afford to abandon the savings now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've advanced the charity our estimated auction takings. Now we just need bidders.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You borrowed five thousand. Only your mum registered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One bidder keeps catering costs down. That's responsible fundraising.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum's only coming to give us a lift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we must bid ourselves. Raise the card limit; protecting that donation has to come first.

D17.editorialNote: Each practical objection becomes a sales argument for the same obviously bad plan.

D18.title: Fake the Expertise
D18.instruction: Perform expertise so confidently that no one questions you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get your boiler running. I know these controls.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've been adjusting the kitchen timer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Establishing the heating interval. Call the engineer; I'll need someone on the boiler.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He asks what temperature you measured.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell him we're still establishing the baseline. Put him on speaker; I'll ask the questions so he can concentrate on readings.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll tune your violin for the audition. I work by ear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've tightened that string until it snapped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That string couldn't hold pitch. I've saved you a failure onstage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The audition panel heard it snap. They're asking if you know what you're doing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them I rejected an unreliable string. Ask for their spare violin; I'll check that one before I approve it.

D18.editorialNote: A invents confident technical interpretations of concrete evidence they do not understand.

D19.title: Everything Is a Contest
D19.instruction: Turn every difference or disagreement into a competition you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I want potatoes; you want pizza. First to peel five chooses. I've done four.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order pizza unless you can find a cheaper dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Potatoes cost nothing. They're already here. I win.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got a voucher. Pizza's free.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then best free dinner wins. I'll cook potatoes, you order pizza, and Mum can judge. She always asks for my potatoes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My tea's stronger than yours. I can handle it without milk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Same teapot. I added milk so I could drink mine sooner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First to finish, then. I've only got two mouthfuls left.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've finished. I'm making another.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fewest refills wins, then. I can make these two mouthfuls last all breakfast.

D19.editorialNote: B's attempt at ordinary cooperation becomes the next measurable contest.

D20.title: Brighter Side
D20.instruction: Meet every setback with even greater optimism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The car won't start. Excellent chance for a walk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's raining.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And a free shower!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My shoe's leaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Brilliant. The shower's finally reached your feet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our show sold no tickets. We can rehearse uninterrupted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The theatre's cancelled us. I'm asking for our deposit back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better! We'll hire the pub upstairs. People already go there voluntarily.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've kept the deposit. All we can afford is the bus home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful—a touring production! I'll carry the scenery; you bring exact change. We can try the opening scene between stops.

D20.editorialNote: Optimism increases as setbacks accumulate, turning each newly lost option into an opportunity.

D21.title: Supportive Rage
D21.instruction: Remain helpful and encouraging while becoming increasingly furious.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've spilled paint on my sofa. Stay there; I'll get a cloth. We can fix this.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's on the carpet too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep blotting. You're doing well. That carpet was my birthday present.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cloth's spreading it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're right. Good catch. Take my clean shirt. I am absolutely furious, but you are not tackling this alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Choose the birthday lunch you really want. I'll drive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The seaside place. We'd lose your deposit here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Forty pounds wasted. Fine. You love the sea; let's make a day of it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked it. They need another forty now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Another forty? Eighty pounds before a bloody sandwich. Give me the number. You're getting your sea view. Ask for a window; you deserve one.

D21.editorialNote: Helpful language remains intact while practical generosity becomes increasingly furious.

D22.title: Terms and Conditions
D22.instruction: Treat every offer, favor, feeling, and apology as a negotiation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll lend you the ladder for two lifts to the station.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only need it for five minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One lift, then. And tell your wife my roses have improved.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I just pay you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Five pounds. Three if you say we're still friends when you hand it over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll accept your apology for missing my birthday if I get first choice of Christmas dates.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum already expects me Christmas Day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Boxing Day, then. In exchange, I'll tell her I'm no longer hurt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd rather you actually stopped being hurt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay through New Year and I'll mean it. I'll even stop mentioning the birthday to Mum.

D22.editorialNote: A negotiates ordinary kindness and even the terms of acceptance as exchanges.

D23.title: Yes, but My Way
D23.instruction: Agree with others, then reinterpret the agreement entirely in your favor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I'll help you move the sofa. I'll take the cushions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're sewn on. We have to lift together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. You lift; I'll say when. Together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need another person underneath it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. I'll book someone on your phone. Then I can give both of you the same countdown.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I'll look after your dog during the kitchen repairs. Bring him over after his walk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He needs to stay overnight too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. Stay in my guest room; you can handle breakfast while I sleep.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can stay, but his six o'clock walk is your job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. I'll organise it: lead by the door, your alarm at five thirty. You won't have to plan a thing.

D23.editorialNote: A verbally agrees, then narrows the agreement to suit their own convenience.

D24.title: The Pattern
D24.instruction: Treat every minor detail as evidence of a much larger problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two office biscuits are missing. We've got an organised operation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ate them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A confession this quick suggests training.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was hungry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they're recruiting through hunger. This goes higher than the biscuit tin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nobody received my meeting email. This office has stopped communicating.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's in your drafts. You forgot to send it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And nobody noticed. Our entire communication system depends on my memory.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send it. Go and have your lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now you're covering communications while I'm absent. We need a succession plan before I take a sandwich.

D24.editorialNote: Minor recurring evidence expands a specific theory of a larger problem, distinct from mere random worry.

S25.title: Default Decision-Maker
S25.instruction: Take charge of every small practical choice, treating speed and efficiency as proof that you should remain in charge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've ordered everyone's sandwiches. We saved six minutes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm vegetarian.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've already removed your ham. Seven minutes saved.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I choose next time?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You could, but I've ordered next time too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Chairs face the window. I've moved them while you were deciding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The speaker's at the other end.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then moving the speaker is quicker than moving twelve chairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's already speaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then everyone turns their own chair. Twelve jobs at once. I'll count you in.

S25.editorialNote: A equates efficient practical choices with a right to make the next choice; B's preferences are treated as delay.

S26.title: Temporary Authority
S26.instruction: Project brisk confidence through the routine, as though any hesitation would reveal that your authority is only temporary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm covering reception until two. Sign here and I'll send you up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The form asks for a visitor badge number.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. We'll issue your badge before we finish the form.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can wait for the receptionist to come back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No waiting. Open those drawers with me. You check left; I'll check right.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: While Miss Bell's out, I'm taking the register. Names, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've got yesterday's list.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. We'll confirm the regulars first. Start at the top.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got today's list. Shall I take over?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand it here. Keep yesterday's open; I'll call for comparisons.

S26.editorialNote: A fills a brief cover shift with confident rules and treats any pause as a threat to legitimacy.

S27.title: There’s a Right Way
S27.instruction: Correct how ordinary tasks are done, emphasizing tiny standards that only a true professional would notice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Those towels need folding with the seams inside.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody sees them in the cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I do. That's why I'm qualified to stack them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I close the cupboard?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After you level the third towel. Doors don't correct technique.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave a finger's width between those mugs in the dishwasher.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've done that. They aren't touching.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use the same finger. You've measured one gap with your thumb.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the middle mug out. Plenty of space now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now centre the other two. You'd never leave gaps like that in a proper hotel.

S27.editorialNote: Tiny technical standards supply the recurring behavior; settings remain consistent throughout each alternative.

S28.title: Regular Around Here
S28.instruction: Act like a longtime insider by recognizing routines, offering shortcuts, and treating unfamiliar details as recent changes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've moved my usual table at this café.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've only opened today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, much fresher since my last visit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What would you like?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My usual. Let's see whether you've changed that too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your first night at the club? I'll show you the shortcut to the cloakroom.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the cleaner's cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They've moved it again. We used to come this way.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sign says it's upstairs. I'll show you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They've restored the original route. You lead; I'll give you the history.

S28.editorialNote: A treats unfamiliarity as a recent local change, preserving the claim to being a regular.

S29.title: Let Me Show You
S29.instruction: Turn each simple task into a lesson. Demonstrate, supervise, and correct as though experience has made you indispensable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me demonstrate how to tie that parcel.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already tied it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Untie it. Learning begins with observation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's going to be opened anyway.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then stay for my lesson on receiving a parcel.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you make tea, watch my wrist with the kettle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've made tea for twenty years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'll appreciate the advanced pour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've finished the tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Now make one under supervision.

S29.editorialNote: A refuses to let competence eliminate a teaching opportunity; the mundane lesson grows increasingly supervised.

S30.title: Keeper of the Details
S30.instruction: Act outwardly helpful while controlling the small information, supplies, or access everyone needs to proceed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Happy to open the supply cupboard. Which project is this for?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We just need batteries.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll need to know which drawer to authorise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We'll buy some.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. I have the petty-cash key too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've got the room bookings. When do you want your meeting?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's empty now. Can we start?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. I'll tell you when the next group needs it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I photograph the list? Then we won't have to bother you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No bother. I'll bring it round when you need to stop. Just concentrate on your meeting.

S30.editorialNote: Small logistical knowledge becomes quiet leverage; B's alternative depends on another detail A controls.

S31.title: Same Old Routine
S31.instruction: Use familiar shorthand and old habits immediately, as though past routines still govern the present.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your chipped mug, my ugly mug. I'll wash; you dry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I bought a dishwasher.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. You load your side; I'll load mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's only one mug rack.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yours on the left, then. Pass me mine when it's done. We always put them away together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two knocks on your window. Ready for our usual walk?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm working from home now. Text first; I might be on a call.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll text 'knock knock.' Same signal. I'll get your walking boots.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've only got ten minutes at lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then straight to our usual bench. I'll bring the sandwiches. Your end, my end.

S31.editorialNote: A immediately operates an old shared routine and reinterprets B's changes as interruptions to it.

S32.title: One More Favor
S32.instruction: Treat every small request as part of a long-running balance sheet of favors, inconveniences, and repayments.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll watch your dog tonight. That settles your fixing my sink.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He just sleeps. Your sink took three hours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave him tomorrow too, then. Two nights for the awkward pipe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave dinner for you. There's lasagne in the fridge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't feed me. I'm trying to get even. If you cook as well, I'll have to take him on holiday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you water my plants? I covered your shift in March.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was one afternoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And these are only six small plants.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One is a tree.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The shift included overtime.

S32.editorialNote: A's favors are itemized by circumstance rather than treated as spontaneous kindness.

S33.title: The Designated Reminder
S33.instruction: Keep track of what everyone was supposed to remember. Supply reminders before being asked and treat forgetfulness as your familiar burden.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've reminded you about the dentist tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's in my calendar.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll remind you to check the calendar.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It sends alerts, but my phone has to stay in my locker.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll remind you at lunch. And remind me to eat mine—no, I'll put that on my list too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bin day tomorrow. I've written it on your breakfast banana.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't always eat breakfast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. I'll put another reminder on the coffee machine. Apparently I track breakfast now too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll set a phone alarm. You can stop leaving notes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll leave one by your charger reminding you what the alarm means.

S33.editorialNote: A turns reminders into a familiar burden and starts monitoring whether reminders themselves will be remembered.

S34.title: Keeping Score
S34.instruction: Treat arrival times, effort, memory, and sacrifice as a running score you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I carried the heavier shopping bag. Again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll carry both bags upstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll put everything away. Carrying gets points, but remembering where things go gets double.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put it away too. You sit down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. I'll count how many times you ask me which cupboard. Those go in my column.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I arrived ten minutes early to help set up. That's ten in my column.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stayed an hour late yesterday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Evenings count differently. Mine required getting out of bed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You live upstairs. I caught the six o'clock bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you were already up. I interrupted actual sleep. We need a separate column for sacrifice.

S34.editorialNote: A scores effort and sacrifice even when B offers to cooperate, keeping a concrete measurable ledger.

S35.title: You Know the System
S35.instruction: Use another person’s knowledge of the routine while pretending you could manage perfectly well alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which counter takes these forms? Just checking they've not moved it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's been counter three for years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. You remember.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Wait. We need a queue ticket before we go over there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Which button gives us counter three? I'm checking they've labelled it sensibly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're opening the allotment shed. Which key do you usually use? I have my own method.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The red one. Lift the handle first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I lift first too. Which way do you turn it afterwards? Comparing methods.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Left. Here, I'll open it; we need the watering cans.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Go ahead. I'll check your sequence against mine. Slowly, though.

S35.editorialNote: A depends on B's routine knowledge but disguises each request as cross-checking or testing.

S36.title: Still About Last Time
S36.instruction: Treat each minor inconvenience as confirmation of an older grievance and the same recurring problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's a sock on the stairs. We've reached this chapter again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I dropped it just now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And last month 'just now' lasted three days.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pick it up. Could you hold my tea?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I'm holding your tea again. Last month I ended up carrying the laundry too. Give me the basket; we're apparently at that bit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Five minutes late for our anniversary dinner. We're doing last year again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The bus broke down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Last year it was a puncture. Dinner always starts with a transport report.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I walked the last mile. I even brought your flowers on foot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Flowers again. Shall I find last year's vase, or are we pretending this is a new apology?

S36.editorialNote: A reads today's small inconvenience as recurrence of a specific unresolved grievance.

S37.title: Must Be Nice
S37.instruction: Treat another person’s ease with ordinary life as both inspiring and unfair. Copy their shortcuts while dismissing the advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Must be nice, cooking dinner in twenty minutes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I chop tomorrow's vegetables while tonight's dinner cooks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pass me tomorrow's carrots, then. Lovely having a whole spare evening inside this one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take half home. Tomorrow you only have to tip them in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take the tub too. Apparently effortless people already have containers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remembered every birthday. Must be nice having that sort of time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I use phone reminders. Here, I'll send you the calendar.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll import it. Some of us remember people because we care.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's also a reminder to buy the cards a week ahead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Turn that on too. Mum calls you thoughtful for obeying your phone. Don't tell her you've sent me this.

S37.editorialNote: A uses the admired shortcut while attributing its success to B's unfairly easy life.

S38.title: We Used to Be Easy
S38.instruction: Treat every practical difficulty as evidence that life, work, or this relationship used to be simpler.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We used to arrange dinner by saying 'dinner?'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now we check six calendars. Thursday at seven works.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me down. We used to manage six people with one shout up the stairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll make it a standing booking. Then nobody has to check again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. A permanent reservation to recreate dropping in. We used to get that for knocking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our old shopping list just said bread, milk, eggs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now we need oat milk for Jo and lactose-free for Dad.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll write both. Milk used to take one line, and we all knew whose it was.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Save the list on your phone. We can reuse it every week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Help me save it, then. We used to finish the list before needing help with it.

S38.editorialNote: A measures practical complexity against an idealised simpler past, keeping one ordinary task in focus.

S39.title: Don’t Be Difficult
S39.instruction: Treat every request, correction, or small inconvenience as a warning that you are becoming too much trouble.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could I get a lift? Only if it isn't trouble.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. I'll move my coat off the passenger seat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't move it for me. I'll sit in the back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's full of shopping. Hold the coat; I'll turn the heating down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please don't change it. I'll keep the coat on my lap. If I get hot, I can get out and walk the rest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could I have another fork? Sorry, this one's bent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. I'll get one from the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please sit down. I shouldn't have made you get up during dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm getting the pudding anyway. It isn't an extra trip.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then just bring pudding. I've already got a spoon. I'll save the peas for another time.

S39.editorialNote: A shrinks each reasonable request after reading neutral logistics as evidence of being burdensome.

S40.title: I Packed for You
S40.instruction: Take care of practical needs before anyone asks, then resist choices that make your preparation unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've packed lunches for your first week at college.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My room doesn't have a fridge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll drop one off every morning. I've labelled the days.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Lunch is included in my fees. I'm meeting my flatmates there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How many flatmates? I'll pack theirs too. You can all meet me outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take this raincoat to the picnic. I checked the forecast all week.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's sunny, and my bag's full.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wear it, then. I didn't spend seven mornings checking so you'd have nothing ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll be boiling. I could sit on it if the grass is wet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll pack a water bottle. We can dampen a patch if necessary.

S40.editorialNote: A's care becomes resistance when B's preference makes the preparation unnecessary.

S41.title: Useful Enough to Stay
S41.instruction: Make yourself constantly useful and read each response as evidence of whether you still belong.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've swept your kitchen. Anything else before I go?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just sit down. You're my guest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The chair could use a polish first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I invited you for company.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll talk while I polish. Two reasons to invite me again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've organised the pens. You'll still need me tomorrow, won't you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Go home; I'm just finishing the rota.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can finish it. Put me wherever there's a gap.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've given you Saturday off. You're part of the team, not emergency cover.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. I'll train the emergency cover on Friday so you won't regret Saturday.

S41.editorialNote: A turns permission to relax into another opportunity to prove useful and retain a place.

S42.title: Notice the Effort
S42.instruction: Make your invisible labor visible through pointed reminders, strategic sighs, and opportunities for appreciation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you put the pizza in, admire the oven. Four hours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's spotless. Can I cook? I'm starving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Notice the rack as you slide it in. That was an hour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll buy you dinner if we can keep it clean tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. We can toast the other three hours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put the empty detergent bottle beside your dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can it move? I need room for my plate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. It represents six loads, if you're wondering.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six? I'll do the laundry tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Come and see how I fold the towels, so you know what you're taking on.

S42.editorialNote: Specific evidence of hidden labor is displayed for appreciation; A seeks recognition rather than the next job.

S43.title: Don’t Break the Routine
S43.instruction: Protect a familiar routine as though changing one step would invite chaos into everything else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tea, then shoes, then keys. You've picked up the keys before we've had tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're late for the train.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we especially need the usual order. Otherwise we'll forget the tickets too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll hold the tickets while you drink.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tickets go in after shoes. Please don't make us start packing again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Curtains, cat food, then our breakfast. Why's his bowl already down?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He woke me early. I fed him so you could sleep.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before the curtains? Now he'll expect every meal before the day starts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll open them now. Your toast is ready too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep it warm. We need him back at the bowl before we can safely have breakfast.

S43.editorialNote: A protects the order itself, restarting the routine when B skips a harmless step.

S44.title: The Contingency Person
S44.instruction: Meet every ordinary problem with a backup plan, emergency supply, or warning about what could happen next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've packed two torches for our picnic, in case we get back after dark.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm carrying lunch uphill. Use our phones and leave the torches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right. I'll bring power banks in case the phones die.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can carry those. My bag's full.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One each, surely. If we get separated, you'd have all the sandwiches and no electricity.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we drive to the campsite, where's the spare jack?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I bought breakdown cover so we could stop packing tools.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll print their number in case your phone dies.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's a garage by the campsite. I'll walk there if necessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then pack your walking boots. And leave me a map, in case I have to come and find you.

S44.editorialNote: Every ordinary precaution requires its own backup, extending one practical chain rather than random catastrophe.

S45.title: Productive Little Disaster
S45.instruction: Treat every mistake or delay as a delightful chance to improve the plan, bond, or discover something better.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The shopping bag split. Lovely, now we can sort dinner before we get home.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The tomatoes are crushed. I wanted sandwiches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've accidentally started pasta sauce. You always say we should cook together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you let me handle the seasoning this time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Try that chilli I always veto. I'll grate the cheese and learn to be surprised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The plumber's cancelled. Lovely, we can finally have lunch together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sink still leaks. I've put a bucket under it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. The bucket's covering the sink; I'll set the table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It needs emptying every ten minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll have courses. Neither of us can rush off with a sandwich.

S45.editorialNote: A uses a mundane failure to invent a specific enjoyable improvement instead of merely declaring optimism.

S46.title: Who’s Cleaning This Up?
S46.instruction: Treat every idea according to the work, cost, cleanup, and follow-through it will create.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Confetti sounds lovely for our wedding. Who's vacuuming it on Monday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll do it. Please let me have the confetti.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then yes. I'll put you down for Monday morning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're flying to Venice at six. I'll ask my brother.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask before we book. I need to know whether I'm packing sandals or the vacuum attachment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You want three extra tables at the party. Who carries them home?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can borrow a van.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who returns the van?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I will. Can we put the deposit on your card?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I need the return time. Those tables are staying on my bill until the van gets home.

S46.editorialNote: A accepts ideas only after assigning their concrete cleanup and follow-through.

S47.title: One Tiny Imperfection
S47.instruction: Choose one tiny imperfection and let it steadily outweigh every larger concern.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we cut our wedding cake, that cherry's stem needs straightening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already called everyone over. Two hundred people are standing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they'll see the top clearly. Turn the stand towards me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Our photographer leaves in two minutes. Please get beside me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask her for a close-up of the stem first. We can have our portrait taken on someone's phone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we hand over the house keys, can we straighten that hallway frame?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The buyers are waiting. Our taxi's outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They're standing right under it. They'll think we left it like that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They just hung it. It's theirs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give them the keys. I'll stay and show them how to look after the frame.

S47.editorialNote: One tiny defect progressively crowds out the important success in the same setting.

S48.title: Nothing Is Ever Simple
S48.instruction: Interpret each new complication as proof that ordinary tasks are secretly designed to become impossible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The wireless printer needs a cable to get started. They lure you in with 'wireless'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just for setup. Then enter the password underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So their next step is turning it upside down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll lift it. You read the label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now their simple setup needs staff. Hold it there; I'll fetch my glasses.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This replacement bulb needs a different fitting. They've made changing a bulb a renovation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's an adapter. I'll order it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's how they get you. The bulb is just the invitation to buy more parts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Delivery's free if we spend another ten pounds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now we have to expand the repair to afford finishing it. What else have they broken?

S48.editorialNote: Each necessary step confirms A's conviction that simple tasks are designed to spawn more tasks.

D25.title: Could You Just…
D25.instruction: Turn a difficult task into tiny favors until the help quietly becomes most of the task.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you hold this shelf bracket against the holes? It keeps slipping.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Briefly. I'm dressed for work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you turn that top screw once? Then you can let go.

beats.speaker: B
