beats.text: It's holding. The other screws are already lined up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just tighten those, then? And slide the shelf onto it to check. I'll get your coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you pinch these bouquet stems together? My wedding ribbon keeps sliding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got them. You need wire underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you twist this bit round, just where your fingers are?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There. That sharp end will snag the dress.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you tuck it in and wind the ribbon over it? One little bow would hide everything. I'll hold the scissors.

D25.editorialNote: One tiny favor expands into the whole task, with each new request growing directly from the previous one.

D26.title: One Last Thing
D26.instruction: Keep someone present by discovering one more small task, question, or favor whenever departure seems near.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you go, could you check this window latch?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's shut. Goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why's the curtain moving?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The fan's on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you show me which switch? There are several.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One last cup to dry before your taxi arrives.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Done. My taxi's here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you reach the shelf for it? I'll fetch your coat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's away. The driver's calling; I really have to go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you put him on speaker first? I should thank him for waiting. What's his name?

D26.editorialNote: A discovers a new concrete reason to delay departure only after B resolves the previous reason.

D27.title: You Could at Least…
D27.instruction: Make the inconvenience visible enough that an apology becomes the easiest way forward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my wet sock beside your dinner. From your puddle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only water.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you won't mind it sharing the table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you move it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An apology would dry the atmosphere considerably.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's the bus timetable. I circled every bus I missed waiting for you to return my keys.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was only twenty minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three circles. And here's the takeaway receipt from when my dinner was still hot.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll buy another dinner. Can we put the papers away?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep your money. Say you're sorry, and we can clear the table instead of reconstructing my evening.

D27.editorialNote: A displays the actual cost of B's inconvenience until an apology becomes the practical response.

D28.title: Just Say Yes
D28.instruction: Get a quick approval before anyone has time to examine the practical consequences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Quick yes to the garden party before the booking expires?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How many guests?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's secure the date, then count chairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And the cost?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll fetch the quote while you say yes. That way we won't lose the booking while you're reading it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just nod and I'll accept the sofa delivery.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will it fit through the door?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can measure after securing the bargain.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's already outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then nod before they start measuring too.

D28.editorialNote: A accelerates a yes before the costly particulars are considered, using the act of reading as a supposed risk.

D29.title: Your Turn
D29.instruction: Get someone to accept responsibility for a task you believe should never have been yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your name's beside bathroom duty. Here's the mop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're better at it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then this is your training opportunity.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you show me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. First, accept the mop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I took your bins out once during your holiday. I didn't volunteer for life. Tonight's yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The neighbours already send you the reminders.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll introduce you in the group as their permanent bin contact.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Stay in it until I know what I'm doing?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll stay until you send 'I'll handle Thursday.' They can welcome you while I leave.

D29.editorialNote: A transfers the responsibility back to its agreed owner, refusing to let competence become permanent duty.

D30.title: What Was the Plan?
D30.instruction: Find out what was promised, scheduled, or changed without revealing that you lost track.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What time did we settle on for Mum's birthday dinner? I'm checking the invitations.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Seven, in the private room. You booked it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. How have you written the restaurant name? I want everything consistent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't written anything. You're doing the invitations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then could you proofread the booking confirmation aloud? I'll type straight from you so we don't introduce any errors.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tomorrow's hike: ridge or river? I'm checking the weather against our route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ridge. We changed because the river path flooded.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Flood warning, then. Where are we meeting? I'll add that to the reminder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've asked me that twice. Have you forgotten your own itinerary?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm checking it works without my help. Brief me like a new recruit; I'll take notes, starting with where I report.

D30.editorialNote: A reconstructs forgotten plans through questions framed as verification, never admitting the lost track.

D31.title: Back Me Up
D31.instruction: Recruit someone to support your version of how an ordinary responsibility should be handled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At the house meeting, back me up about the bins being Alex's turn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought it was yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only on the old rota. Remember the new conversation?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There was a new conversation?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're having it now. Try to remember it confidently.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell the manager we agreed I'd cover the morning, not the evening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wasn't in that meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you have no conflicting memory.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not lying for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you look thoughtfully unsurprised while I explain?

D31.editorialNote: A recruits support for a disputed everyday arrangement and negotiates the wording of that support.

D32.title: Try It First
D32.instruction: Get someone else to test the shortcut, substitute, or questionable fix before you rely on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Turn the kitchen tap on before I start washing up. I've tightened the loose joint.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It sprayed me last time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wear my apron. I need to know whether the joint holds.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You wear it and turn the tap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll need it dry for washing up. You can have my raincoat for the test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Taste this cheap coffee substitute before I fill my cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We still have proper coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If you like this, we can save the proper stuff for guests.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not sacrificing breakfast to save you money.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One sip. If it's awful, I'll buy you a croissant and keep my cup empty.

D32.editorialNote: A coaxes B into testing an uncertain shortcut while remaining ready to learn from the result.

D33.title: Count What I Did
D33.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the practical work, time, or inconvenience you contributed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you call that a quick shop, I carried twelve bags up six flights.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I know. Sit down; I'll put everything away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. The frozen peas came up separately. That was a second trip.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you sit down twice. I'll make tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you tell everyone why I'm getting two rests? Otherwise it looks like one long sit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I spent my Saturday fixing your fence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only three panels.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three panels, eighteen screws, two shops and one blister.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll recommend you to next door. They've got six panels.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them three took my whole Saturday before you make me sound available for Sunday.

D33.editorialNote: A insists that effort be recognized in its concrete units rather than dismissed as a minor favor.

D34.title: Pick a Priority
D34.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your parents' gravy needs stirring and you need a lift to the station. Which am I doing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't you leave dinner on a timer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It won't stir the gravy. Do I finish their dinner or drive you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finish dinner. I'll book a taxi. Just carry my suitcase downstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose again: suitcase downstairs now, or gravy without lumps for your parents?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The parcel depot closes at six. Your mother's waiting outside the station. Which am I collecting?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The parcel's her birthday present.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then do you want her waiting for me or waiting for her present?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Get the parcel. I'll call her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She's calling me now. Shall I pull over to explain, or keep driving before the depot shuts?

D34.editorialNote: Two incompatible obligations force B to choose what will be sacrificed; A refuses a vague demand for both.

D35.title: Move It for Me
D35.instruction: Get someone to rearrange an ordinary commitment as proof that your relationship takes priority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Move your haircut so we can have lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked it for weeks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've been friends since school. Couldn't I have its place just once?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They charge twenty pounds if I change it today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll pay. Put lunch in that exact slot, in pen. You've used pencil for me since school.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you leave quiz night for your sister's first exhibition opening?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm captain. They'll think I've abandoned them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them your sister needs you. I'd like that to outrank geography.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave after round one and say I've got a headache.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come after round one, but tell them it's for me. I want to rank above geography, not below a headache.

D35.editorialNote: A asks for a small rescheduling as evidence of personal priority, not simply availability.

D36.title: Hand It Over
D36.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me fix that cupboard hinge. The door's lower than when you started.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm just finding the right screw.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've tried four. Give me the screwdriver while you find it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you'll tell everyone you fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can announce the repair. I'll stand behind you with the screwdriver, keeping the door attached.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me handle the seating plan. You've put the exes together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're civil now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they can be civil from separate tables.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've spent hours on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the pencil. I'll preserve the hours and move the chairs.

D36.editorialNote: A seeks control of a task by offering a concrete handover while B keeps defending ownership.

D37.title: Put It Back Quietly
D37.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put your umbrella back in the stand. You'll want it for work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is it wet? It hasn't rained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I gave it a rinse. I'll dry the handle before you go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's pondweed caught in the spokes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it needs another rinse. Have breakfast; I'll get it back in the stand properly this time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your plate's back in the cupboard, ready for Sunday lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That one's got flowers. Ours were plain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take that one. The potatoes will cover the flowers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not hiding it under potatoes. I want six matching plates.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get five more before lunch. Keep the plain ones for spares; there's no need to count those today.

D37.editorialNote: A restores an object inconspicuously while new evidence threatens to reveal the original misuse.

D38.title: Talk Around the Mess
D38.instruction: Keep attention on minor details so no one addresses the larger responsibility you avoided.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum's coming for lunch. Is this spoon clean enough for her?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The spoon's fine. You haven't cleaned the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She checks cutlery. Could you check the forks while I finish this?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've told her to bring rubber gloves and help you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we need a guest towel. Can you help me choose one without a faded stripe?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which label colour suits these boxes?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You haven't packed them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good labels prevent moving-day confusion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The van's outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'd better choose a colour the driver likes.

D38.editorialNote: A directs attention to minor presentable details so a major unfinished responsibility stays unaddressed.

D39.title: Spare Them the Hassle
D39.instruction: Hide a practical problem because you believe handling it alone is kinder than involving anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit down, love. You've been on the ward all night. I'll bring lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why's there a bucket by my chair?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just catching a drip. Take the sofa; I've made you a tray.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll eat upstairs and go straight to bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay here. I'll bring your duvet down; upstairs needs a little drying before I put your bed back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Enjoy your afternoon off. Your bike will be ready for tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why's the repair shop asking me to collect a wheel?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They've got your number on the ticket. I'll collect everything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A wheel? Is the rest at another shop?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only until four. Stay with your book; I've planned a route that gets all of it home before you need it.

D39.editorialNote: A hides an inconvenient problem to spare B worry and quietly increases their own burden.

D40.title: Who Changed It?
D40.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Interesting. The picnic moved from Saturday to Friday. Whose blue pen is that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine, but everyone uses it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And whose handwriting adds hearts to Fridays?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right, I changed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Now, who should tell the Saturday guests?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can't open the cupboard. Was the sofa this close yesterday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's more room for yoga now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did making that room involve moving the sofa?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, I moved it. I put the things you'll need somewhere easier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How thoughtful. Would those be the mugs in your sock drawer, or has someone else improved the kitchen too?

D40.editorialNote: Innocent detail questions narrow responsibility for a changed shared plan until a voluntary admission becomes likely.

D41.title: Basically Finished
D41.instruction: Describe incomplete, late, or improvised work as a thoughtful version of completion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your cupboard's finished. I've left the shelves loose so you can choose the heights.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They fall down. You haven't fitted the supports.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's complete as an adjustable kit. Position everything around your tins.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I paid you to install it. Here's the drill.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll fasten one shelf at your chosen height. A finished sample, so you can approve the rest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's the finished budget report. Just the title page: I've left room for contributions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The board meets in ten minutes. They need your figures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's the discussion edition. They can supply their figures directly, without reading mine first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The chair wants a recommendation, not a discussion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll add 'Approve' beneath the title. Finished decision edition. We've eliminated the discussion entirely.

D41.editorialNote: Incomplete work is described as an intentional finished product; practical testing exposes what remains absent.

D42.title: I’ve Done This Before
D42.instruction: Perform calm familiarity with the task while learning how it works from every new clue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll make your coffee. I know this machine: this button starts it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's steam. The coffee button is behind the flap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. Steam first, then the concealed coffee controls. Where's your cup?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here. It makes two cups unless you turn that dial.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Dial to one. I always tailor the standard procedure to the guest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll have this tent up before the rain. I'm familiar with these sleeves.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This one has clips. The poles cross first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, the clip system. Cross the poles; then we attach the fabric.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That fabric's the outer cover. We're standing on the inner tent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Step off the inner tent and we'll raise it first. I always lay everything out.

D42.editorialNote: A learns from B's practical corrections while pretending to recall each step from experience.

D43.title: Outdo the Effort
D43.instruction: Answer every favor, chore, or sacrifice with a bigger one that restores your lead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You brought soup? I'll cook your dinners all week.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're ill. I've already filled your freezer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then when I'm better, I'll fill yours twice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's tiny. Just return the tubs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll bring them back full, with a bigger freezer. That should put me ahead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thanks for the lift. I'll cover your Saturday shift.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No need. I covered yours yesterday so you could rest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll take your whole weekend. You shouldn't be doing more than me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already swapped Sunday to drive you to the airport.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll cancel my flight and cover your holiday. You deserve the longer break.

D43.editorialNote: A exceeds the actual favor just offered, turning generosity into competitive escalation.

D44.title: Efficiency Win
D44.instruction: Celebrate each inconvenience as proof that a faster, cheaper, or smarter routine can now be invented.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The lift's broken. We can cancel the gym and use the stairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We live eight floors up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A full programme included in the rent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How do we carry the shopping?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Resistance training. We've saved two memberships.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The dishwasher's broken. Excellent: we'll serve the curry in rolls. No plates to wash.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are twelve guests and only six rolls.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Halve them. Open sandwiches: twice the servings, same bread.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The curry will run off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hollow them out first. Edible bowls, and the crumbs thicken the curry. We've saved the flour too.

D44.editorialNote: A derives a concrete efficiency scheme from each inconvenience rather than celebrating without a plan.

D45.title: No Trouble at All
D45.instruction: Remain gracious and accommodating while making your growing inconvenience impossible to miss.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course your brother can stay for dinner. I'll give him my pie.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You haven't eaten either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please don't worry. There are peas, and I had a substantial breakfast.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order you a pizza. It takes forty minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How thoughtful. I'll keep everyone company while they eat, then you can all watch me have dinner at nine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll carry your book bag to the platform. My shoulder should manage one more staircase.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let me take it. There are dictionaries in there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, keep your hands free for the tickets. I'll change shoulders at the bottom.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've moved our train to platform twelve, across the bridge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, lead the way. I'll give each shoulder a staircase and rest my fingers while you find our seats.

D45.editorialNote: A accommodates each extra burden while ensuring the cost remains impossible to overlook.

D46.title: Fair Exchange
D46.instruction: Price every favor in time, effort, inconvenience, or future obligation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll wash up if you do two shopping trips.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Two trips for one pan?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This pan has dried cheese. Rates have changed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll soak it first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then one trip and the detergent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Half an hour helping you move buys two hours painting my shed on Saturday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Saturday's my only lie-in. Can I come after lunch?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Afternoon painting costs me cricket. Three hours, then.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll hire a painter. But I need the sofa carried up three flights.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then two painter-hours covers loading; the stairs cost a third. Cricket's free again.

D46.editorialNote: The price of a favor is recalculated in concrete time and effort when B challenges the exchange.

D47.title: Technically, Yes
D47.instruction: Comply with every agreement in the narrowest possible way while insisting you honored it completely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You asked me to move a box. I've moved this one beside the van. All done.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant all twenty boxes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Happy to move all twenty beside it. That completes the revised request.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They need to be inside the van.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. I'll put them just inside the doors. You didn't ask me to leave room for the sofa.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I watered the fern you pointed at. Your holiday watering is done.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant every plant, every day until Sunday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. One teaspoon per plant each day through Sunday. That covers them all.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Use a full can on each. And empty the saucers afterwards.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. I'll empty the saucers on Sunday. You specified daily watering, not daily emptying.

D47.editorialNote: A fulfills the literal minimum of an agreement and treats B's broader expectation as a new request.

D48.title: One Thing Leads to Another
D48.instruction: Use each small problem to justify solving a broader, more disruptive problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This dripping tap is our chance to replace the whole sink.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only needs a washer. I've bought one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. We'll fit it while the sink's out and replace that swollen worktop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The worktop runs under every cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll empty the kitchen. With the cupboards out, we can finally fix the layout.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This café chair wobbles. Let's take all the chairs apart and check their joints.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I tested them. It's only this chair, on this floorboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll lift the floorboards. The chairs have exposed a flooring problem.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're opening in twenty minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll close for renovations. Once the floor's up, we can move the counter and sort out the queue.

D48.editorialNote: A turns a small repair into a progressively larger intervention through a consistent chain of supposed dependencies.

S49.title: The Final Word
S49.instruction: Treat every opinion you offer as a ruling and every continued discussion as an appeal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Green suits our hallway. That's settled; I'll get the rollers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I live here too. Can we try my blue sample?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your appeal can have one square beside the radiator.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. We'll ask our daughter which she prefers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She can hear the appeal. I'll explain why green won before you show her the square.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've decided we order soup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're choosing our own lunches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your appeal is denied. Separate bills don't overturn the soup ruling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already paid for a sandwich.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'm amending the ruling to include a starter. Order the soup before they bring your sandwich.

S49.editorialNote: Opinions become rulings and ordinary disagreement becomes a formal appeal.

S50.title: Conditional Command
S50.instruction: Project firm authority, then soften whenever the source of that authority might be questioned.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All deliveries go round the back. You'll have to move that trolley.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did the building manager approve that? This fridge barely fits the front door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can make an exception for your fridge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll show her your badge and ask where she wants it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's keep her out of the lifting. You choose the entrance; I'll take the heavy end.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm setting the rehearsal order. Solos first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did the director ask you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She values initiative. We could begin with your solo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No need. An ensemble opening suddenly feels more inclusive.

S50.editorialNote: A retreats tactically when asked who authorized their power, then tries to preserve the appearance of command.

S51.title: The Gatekeeper
S51.instruction: Use expertise and standards to decide who is qualified to judge, participate, or proceed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before joining our cheese panel, identify this rind.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I just came to eat cheese.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then identify it for the tasting queue. Judging requires the county certificate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have that certificate. I teach the county course.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Before you examine our cheese, let me examine your syllabus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may judge the garden competition once I check your pruning certificate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm filling in for my wife. She's broken her ankle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then show me where you'd cut this rose. We can assess you here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She could judge by video. I'll carry the phone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. First demonstrate that you can distinguish a diseased leaf from a blurry one.

S51.editorialNote: Participation depends on A's expert eligibility standard, which expands when B tries to discuss the standard itself.

S52.title: Rightful Place
S52.instruction: Carry yourself as the rightful holder of your role and treat any demand for proof as an insult.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why is someone sitting in my chair at the founders' dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's a sponsor. Have you brought your founder's invitation?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You need an envelope to establish that I founded this place?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I know you did. I'll bring another chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For him, thank you. Put mine back at the head.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my nameplate on the allotment committee chair. Let's start.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Have you got the result sheet? I need to verify who's chairing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You want me to prove I'm entitled to my own chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call the secretary. She can confirm it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put her on speaker. Once she's confirmed me, I'll ask her to minute your apology.

S52.editorialNote: A regards an ordinary proof requirement as an affront to a role they consider inherently theirs.

S53.title: The Crown Must Pass
S53.instruction: Treat another person as your likely successor. Prepare them to lead, then reclaim authority whenever their independence makes your influence feel temporary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's the café key. Your first day in charge. I'll watch quietly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm opening an hour later. You won't have to come in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Check timetable changes with me first. Regulars need continuity.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll explain it to them myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good practice. I'll stand beside you and handle any questions about the hours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my chair, deputy. Lead the meeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: First, staff rotas won't need your approval anymore.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent confidence. I'll need to approve that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already told the staff to send their rotas directly to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell them I'll do the final review beside you. You should see how approval works before abolishing it.

S53.editorialNote: A prepares a successor but takes back control as soon as succession looks real.

S54.title: The Quiet Veto
S54.instruction: Remain pleasant and cooperative while behaving as though nothing can proceed without your private consent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd love your exhibition to happen. I haven't signed the room form yet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The installer needs it by four. Is there anything I can change?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nothing. It's lovely. I just need to feel ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll book the other gallery. They don't need your signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll gladly introduce you. Let me approve the email before you send it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The youth club trip sounds wonderful. I've helped finish the coach booking.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thanks. We just need your funding code.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll send it when I'm comfortable releasing it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sit with you while you check the figures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How kind. The figures are fine. You can help me write a reassuring update while everyone waits.

S54.editorialNote: A remains agreeable while withholding the concrete consent needed to proceed.

S55.title: We Started Equal
S55.instruction: Use shared beginnings to erase present rank, titles, and attempts to place distance between you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We started on the same biscuit-packing line. Pass the biscuits, Director.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please use my title at work. The new staff are here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. This is the director. We shared my lunch when he forgot his.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you tell them something more recent?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He's sharing today. Pass that tin, mate; I'll do the introductions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've pulled my chair beside yours for the induction. Like our first day.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm introducing myself as their manager.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll introduce us together. We spent our first morning looking for the toilets.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. You show them around after my welcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come with me. You found the toilets; I found the kitchen. We still make one useful employee.

S55.editorialNote: Shared beginnings erase present rank; A treats new formal distance as a betrayal of old equality.

S56.title: My Support, My Say
S56.instruction: Treat every past favor as a continuing investment in your right to influence present decisions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I bought your bakery mixer. Save me a place at the menu tasting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a birthday gift, not a share in the bakery.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I backed your cakes. I should taste what my support produces.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're switching to bread. Come Friday; the customers will choose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll come Thursday. They should only choose between loaves I've approved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before changing the club name, remember who paid the deposit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've paid you back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The money, yes. I still backed the club we're naming.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The printer needs a name today. Pick between these two.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me see the rejected names too. My support deserves more than the final round.

S56.editorialNote: Past support is treated as an ongoing investment that purchases current decision-making rights.

S57.title: The Trusted Deputy
S57.instruction: Act as the reliable second-in-command, managing access and details while quietly shaping every decision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As assistant director, I've costed both sets. The garden fits our budget.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So does my kitchen. Give the director both designs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. I'll put the garden sketch on the cover to brighten the pack.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Use a plain cover. We can each present our design.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll schedule you both. The garden designer can go first while you're setting up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The captain's finishing her briefing. As first mate, I'm collecting harbor updates.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: North harbor's closed. South and west both have berths available.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll flag the closure immediately and attach my recommendation for west.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll report the options myself. I haven't recommended either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. I'll introduce you and bring both berth sheets. West's booking form is already filled in; I'll leave it beside her pen.

S57.editorialNote: A controls a leader's choices through access and presentation while insisting they are merely assisting.

S58.title: The Succession Race
S58.instruction: Treat every success, mistake, and compliment as evidence in an ongoing contest over who should lead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I fixed the office kettle. Put that in my column for next manager.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no vacancy. Sam bought the replacement fuse.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give Sam procurement. Give me delivery.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You two could fix the toaster together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. I'll coordinate Sam. We can finally compare technical ability with leadership.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sam's missed the stock meeting. Another point to me for next manager.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's unloading the delivery. Cancel the meeting and help him.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll record my attendance, then my flexibility.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam asked for you specifically. He says you're good at stacking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put that under endorsements. I'll stack beside him so we can see whose pile stays up.

S58.editorialNote: Everyday outcomes become a succession dossier, even before any vacancy exists.

S59.title: Indispensable Rival
S59.instruction: Use another person’s judgment constantly while minimizing how much influence that dependence gives them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Check my wedding speech again. Just punctuation this time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Cut the divorce joke. The bride's parents separated last month.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, that's why I flagged it. What should replace it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Use my story about them getting lost on their first date. Credit me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll thank you for proofreading. How does your story end?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which road gets us to the wedding? I'm checking my choice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: East. The west bridge is closed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As I thought. Which east turn?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Give me the map and let me navigate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can hold it. I'll make the decisions. Is this the turn?

S59.editorialNote: A relies on a rival's judgment while denying the influence and taking public ownership.

S60.title: Once Undermined
S60.instruction: Treat every disagreement as a possible repeat of the moment your authority was previously weakened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Last time someone moved lunch, they held the meeting without me. Why move it again?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sandwich delivery's late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what they said while electing my replacement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then we'll eat in here. You can keep chairing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Put the sandwiches beside me. Last time everyone followed whoever had the platter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You crossed out my tea order, Pat. Last year it was my shed proposal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We only need twenty cups. You ordered forty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's how the committee started calling my judgment unreliable.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll write that the attendance changed. This isn't a vote on you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Put that last sentence in the minutes too.

S60.editorialNote: A interprets small disagreement through a concrete past undermining, escalating procedural defenses.

S61.title: Power Looks Good
S61.instruction: Act fascinated by confident behavior; imitate it closely while resenting how naturally it seems to work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your pause silenced the committee. I'll copy it for my report. Annoying how easily that works for you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was holding back a cough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even your cough commands respect. How long did you hold it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just say, 'I'd like your attention.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like your attention. Was that your exact tone? You make four words look hereditary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You got us this table with one raised eyebrow. Show me. Must be nice having that face.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I raised the left one. But please just ask for the bill; I'm late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Left. Like this? You barely moved yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's coming. Keep it there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You got a table in a second. I'm getting a cramp asking for paper.

S61.editorialNote: A imitates another's confident technique while resenting its ease, visibly adjusting the same borrowed behavior.

S62.title: Formerly Important
S62.instruction: Carry the habits and expectations of a role that once made you important, even when the present no longer supports them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've brought my headteacher's bell to the retirement lunch. Shall I ring everyone into their seats?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please sit down. I promised the caterers we'd start at one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me the register. I'll find who's holding us up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a buffet. Your former colleagues can serve themselves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll appoint table monitors. They can report to me before anyone takes seconds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring the shop takings over. I've put out my counting tray.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You sold me the shop last year. I count them now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Bring your total and I'll check it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I came to invite you to our anniversary sale.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Already a year? Leave me the proposed discounts. I'll approve them before you print.

S62.editorialNote: An old office habit persists after the role ends; A treats lost power as a technical inconvenience.

S63.title: One Mistake from Gone
S63.instruction: Treat every decision as a test of whether you still deserve your place.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First lunch as supervisor. If I order soup, will they think promoting me was a mistake?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I promoted you. I'm having soup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then soup. Unless copying you proves I can't lead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Choose mine too. I need to take this call.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Both lunches? Right. Does choosing the bread count toward whether I keep the job?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've signed the delivery form. Was my signature managerial enough?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It just needs to be legible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So they've lowered the standard for me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No, it's the same form.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll practise until I deserve the same form.

S63.editorialNote: A treats a trivial new decision as proof of continued suitability and seeks escalating verification.

S64.title: Protection Has Terms
S64.instruction: Treat safety, support, and reassurance as arrangements that require you to remain in control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Borrow my car. I'll feel better if we agree every stop first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just my sister's, then home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Text before leaving hers so I can approve the traffic.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She might need me to stay overnight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Give me her number; I'll arrange your bedtime so you're safe to drive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll fund your exhibition. Let me choose the guests so nobody undermines you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need critics there. That's how I get another show.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send me their names. I'll find the encouraging ones.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The main critic won't promise a good review.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll sit beside her. You can concentrate on being independent while I handle her questions.

S64.editorialNote: Support is offered as a conditional arrangement that keeps A in supervisory control.

S65.title: Chosen by Power
S65.instruction: Seek the attention of whoever seems influential and treat that attention as proof that you belong.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The mayor said hello. That means I can sit at her table, doesn't it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm seating donors. She says hello to everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Introduce me again. If she remembers me, you'll know I belong there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's asked you to bring over that empty chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She picked me. I'll carry it over and ask which side of her I should sit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me beside the director in the group photo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm photographing her team. She only asked you to hold her coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell her my name. She should know who she's trusting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now she wants you to bring her bag to the car. You're blocking my shot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take both. Ask if she wants me beside her in the car. She clearly needs me on the team.

S65.editorialNote: A treats influential attention as proof of inclusion, trying to convert incidental contact into public affiliation.

S66.title: Public Respect
S66.instruction: Seek visible signs of respect and treat private appreciation as insufficient.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your note about my rescue of the accounts was lovely. Will you read it at the staff lunch?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wrote it privately because you hate speeches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Giving them. Hearing one about my work is quite different.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no microphone. I can thank you at our table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Let's move our table into the middle so nobody misses your thanks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you introduce me as Chair at the committee picnic?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thanked you for chairing when you arrived.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Very warmly. Unfortunately, everyone else was unpacking.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask you to pass the sandwiches. They'll hear your name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say, 'Our Chair will now serve lunch.' Then I'll wait for them to look up.

S66.editorialNote: Private appreciation is insufficient; A seeks a public, correctly framed display of respect.

S67.title: Chain of Command
S67.instruction: Treat every question, favor, and decision as something that must travel through the proper hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your request for a teaspoon must go through the kitchen supervisor.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're standing beside the teaspoons.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Physical proximity is not authority.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the kitchen supervisor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then countersign your request. I'll pass it up to catering.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I lend you this ladder, your department head must ask mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're neighbours, cleaning gutters. My wife sent me over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then her request should go to my wife. I can supply the ladder's dimensions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your wife's away. She left you in charge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then address it to me as acting head. I'll forward it to her for confirmation.

S67.editorialNote: An ordinary request is routed through an escalating hierarchy, not just used as an avoidance objective.

S68.title: Power Vacuum
S68.instruction: Treat any uncertainty about who is in charge as an emergency that must be resolved immediately.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nobody's chairing this picnic. We can't open the hamper.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can decide together. I just want everyone fed before the games.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Together isn't a name. The children are opening crisps—who can tell them to wait?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine, you're in charge of lunch. Sam's running the games.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stop his whistle. Who's in charge if a game runs into lunch? We need one name now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The manager's gone. Wait—who's in charge of the kettle?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Anyone. I'll make tea while you lock up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you're in charge. I'll tell everyone before I touch the doors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only until my taxi comes. It's outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Name your replacement before you get in. We can't have boiling water between administrations.

S68.editorialNote: An empty leadership position becomes the emergency; attempts at shared decisions create another authority question.

S69.title: Opportunity for Influence
S69.instruction: Find a path to greater influence in every assignment, setback, or unexpected responsibility.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put me on the broken printer? I'll need purchasing authority.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It just needs paper. There's a box by my desk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll move it to mine and manage supplies.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. Then everyone will come to you when they run out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Have them bring their print jobs too, so I can decide which ones get priority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The tenants rejected my bike shed proposal? I'll chair the review.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No review. Just send everyone the result; I need to book next month's meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll collect replies too. You need someone who knows what residents want.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine, but you'll have to read forty emails.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll draft your agenda. I'll know which complaints deserve the meeting's time.

S69.editorialNote: A turns each undesirable task or setback into a specific expansion of influence.

S70.title: Who Can Authorize This?
S70.instruction: Treat titles and speeches as secondary; focus on who can grant access, allocate resources, and create consequences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely ribbon-cutting. Our freezer delivery is outside; who can unlock the building?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The chief executive wants us both in the photograph first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can she let the freezers in? Photograph us while she unlocks.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only the caretaker has keys. He's leaving in her car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep her posing, then. I'll get the caretaker to open up before she needs her car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your title's impressive. Can you release the repair funds?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My deputy handles finance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then may I speak to the powerful part of this office?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I make the big decisions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Decide to introduce me to the cheque book.

S70.editorialNote: A ignores symbolic rank and follows the concrete power to unlock, pay or authorize.

S71.title: Symbol of Office
S71.instruction: Choose one symbol, privilege, or position and treat control of it as proof of legitimate authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm wearing the barbecue apron. I decide when the burgers turn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my apron.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you should respect its office.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take it back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That would be a transfer of power. Finish your petition first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I have the meeting bell. That means I'm chairing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a bicycle bell.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And yet you stopped talking when I rang it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I borrow it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After I finish deciding whether you may.

S71.editorialNote: Possession of a small symbol becomes A's basis for legitimate authority, even when the symbol is trivial.

S72.title: Invisible Hierarchy
S72.instruction: Treat every interaction as evidence of an unseen hierarchy and keep identifying who truly outranks whom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You fetched her coffee. So she's above you on the chart.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was being nice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Unpaid tribute. A very secure position for her.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She fetched mine yesterday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then this is a rotating monarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Everyone looked at the quiet man before approving the budget. He must run this place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's the electrician. The lights flickered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And the director waited for his nod. So he's above her.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's stopping the meeting to let him out. Can we please finish?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Once she returns. Apparently even his departure outranks our budget.

S72.editorialNote: A reads an ordinary exchange as evidence of hidden rank and updates a hierarchy from each new clue.

D49.title: Make Them Your Deputy
D49.instruction: Get someone’s help by defining it as service under your direction.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need help running the raffle. I've made you a deputy badge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why not co-organiser?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because I need help, not a second direction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What does the deputy do?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Everything I can confidently delegate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come organise the picnic as my second-in-command.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We could share the work equally.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. You execute half; I direct all of it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That isn't equal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your first assignment is improving the wording.

D49.editorialNote: A secures help by inventing a subordinate role and preserves the hierarchy when B proposes equality.

D50.title: Not Dismissed
D50.instruction: Keep someone present by treating departure as a privilege only you can grant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The shop's shut, but wait by the till until I dismiss you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've counted it. My daughter's waiting outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring her in. I can check the cash while you help with her homework.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's finished it. Our taxi's here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll finish your dismissal in the taxi. You may sit down, but tell him departure still needs my approval.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you put your coat on, I'd like to formally conclude our coffee.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only stopped for ten minutes. My bus is due.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll consider an early departure. Sit down while I decide.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The café's closing. They've asked us both to leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. We'll wait outside together. Their permission to leave doesn't replace mine.

D50.editorialNote: A treats a normal departure as a release they personally grant, continually redefining when that release applies.

D51.title: Acknowledge the Disrespect
D51.instruction: Make someone apologize for the disrespect to your position, not merely for what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your apology should mention interrupting the chair, not just spilling the tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry about your trousers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The trousers hold no office.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry I interrupted you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: 'Chair.' Let's repair the title while we're here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You told the trainees their head trainer was an idiot. I want an apology.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry your drill failed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For undermining their head trainer. They still need to follow my instructions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll email them after tomorrow's drill.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read it to them before the drill. My whistle isn't going to outrank 'idiot' on its own.

D51.editorialNote: A redirects apology away from the practical incident toward the affront to A's rank.

D52.title: Secure the Endorsement
D52.instruction: Get a visible endorsement that makes your decision or position harder to challenge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Would you endorse the new rota into this microphone?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I already said it was fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Quietly. Quietly can't protect me at the staff meeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I email you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Copy everyone who might blame me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sign here to say you support the extension.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I like it, but I'd rather not put my name down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then your support has no address when objections arrive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I use initials?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only if we print the key beside them.

D52.editorialNote: A seeks support in a public durable form that will survive later disagreement.

D53.title: Delegate Downward
D53.instruction: Make someone accept an unwanted responsibility by placing them lower in the hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As junior coordinator, you're responsible for the blocked sink.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ran the whole event yesterday. You said I'd earned a promotion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: To senior coordinator. Still below me, but now you can supervise the plumber.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He can only come after everyone leaves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'll lock up too. I can't give building security to a junior.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're my deputy. You'll answer the inspector's complaints.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Most of them concern decisions you made.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. You handle the details below decision-making level.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The inspector wants whoever signs the replies at tomorrow's hearing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sign as deputy, then. You can represent me without giving the impression we're equals.

D53.editorialNote: An unwanted task is assigned as proof of junior rank, and every objection is reframed as a developmental duty.

D54.title: Find the Real Authority
D54.instruction: Probe until you know who can approve, block, or reverse the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I book the trip, who can still cancel it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The committee approved it. Please book before we lose the coach.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Whose objection would stop you paying the deposit?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The treasurer's. But she's away, and her deputy has the bank login.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can the deputy release it alone, or does she still need the treasurer's permission?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The pipe's still leaking. Which signature releases the repair money?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All three. I've spent all morning getting them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could anyone still freeze it after your morning's work?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finance could. Though they unfroze the roof payment when the caretaker called.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What did the caretaker have: permission to overrule finance, or someone else's direct number?

D54.editorialNote: A follows authority past titles to the person who can actually stop or reverse the decision.

D55.title: Build a Coalition
D55.instruction: Recruit someone to your side so your position appears broader and more legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit with me for the allotment shed vote. It shouldn't look like just my project.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only support it if everyone gets a key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Shared keys. Agreed. Will you join me now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The new plot holders need to hear that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring them over. We can present it together as the shared-access proposal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you join my request to keep the pottery room open late? It looks like a personal favour with one name.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I leave at five.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your name would show it's bigger than the evening class.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The morning class wants weekend access.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Add that. Could you bring two of them? We'd be several classes asking for better access.

D55.editorialNote: A builds visible support before agreement is settled, bargaining down from endorsement to appearance.

D56.title: Challenge by Proxy
D56.instruction: Persuade someone else to challenge a rule or authority before you risk doing it yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask the director why the overtime rule changed. I'll support you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why don't you ask?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your fresh perspective won't carry my disciplinary history.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you stand beside me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just behind. Where supportive people remain employable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you challenge the captain's queue-jumping rule at tonight's club meeting?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He cancelled my booking last time I complained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask him to restore your booking as well. I'll draft both requests for your speech.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then sign it. I want him to know it's both of us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll leave space for my signature. Once he's agreed you have a point, call me up to add it.

D56.editorialNote: A recruits a proxy challenge and carefully negotiates how visible their own support will be.

D57.title: Use the Proper Title
D57.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your standing through a title, privilege, courtesy, or public sign of respect.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At the staff barbecue, introduce me as Director Patel.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm introducing everyone by first name. Even the owner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me a separate introduction when I welcome the staff.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The owner's doing the welcome. You offered to serve burgers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then introduce the burger service: 'Director Patel will serve you.' I'd like them to hear who's making this gesture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My place card should say Chairperson, not simply Jo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone knows you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then nobody will struggle with the extra word.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no room on the card.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use the larger plate.

D57.editorialNote: A insists on a specific courtesy and escalates from a missed word to a visible status marker.

D58.title: Declare Allegiance
D58.instruction: Make someone choose which person, side, or claim to authority they will support.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For the workshop move, are you backing my proposal or Morgan's?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your location, Morgan's budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. Whose proposal will you call that in the meeting?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call it a compromise.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And when Morgan and I both claim you supported us, which one will you correct?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you wear my ribbon or Nina's for the chess club election?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Neither. You're both my friends.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep us both as friends. Which one do you want as chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I wear yours today and hers tomorrow?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tomorrow's the vote. Tell me which ribbon you'll wear then; I'll happily lend you the other one today.

D58.editorialNote: A turns partial agreement or neutrality into a demand to choose whose authority to support.

D59.title: Obey Without Explanation
D59.instruction: Create increasingly inconvenient requests that test whether someone accepts your authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring that empty box to my desk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What do you need it for?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At present, to establish whether you'll bring it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Take it back without the question this time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave your desk and stand by that open window.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need to know whether my team follows a direct request.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's freezing. Can I get my coat?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Fetch mine too, then come back and hold it while I check the rest of the team.

D59.editorialNote: Trivial tasks become increasingly inconvenient tests of obedience; A refuses to supply a practical reason.

D60.title: Pass Me the Authority
D60.instruction: Get someone to transfer authority publicly by naming you as the person who decides what happens next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand me the hall key and tell everyone I'm now in charge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I just give you the key? My retirement taxi's waiting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The door will understand. The committee needs words.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're outside asking me whether to cancel Saturday's dance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them I decide whether it goes ahead. Then ask me, in front of them. Your taxi can be my first approval.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before leaving the meeting, name me as the person who decides.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're sitting in my chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Furniture announces location, not succession.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. You're chairing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: To the room, please. I already agree.

D60.editorialNote: A seeks a public transfer of decision-making, not merely possession of a useful object.

D61.title: Orders from the Shadows
D61.instruction: Hide that you set the problem in motion while quietly directing how everyone responds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The crates went to Leeds. Send the driver to me; I'll sort it quietly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your email says Leeds. Shall I forward it to the manager?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Forward my corrected address instead. She needs the destination, not the correspondence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She wants a timeline before approving another van.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with when we discovered the error. I'll arrange the van while you write.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll rebuild the wedding bookings. Could you reassure the couples?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cancellation log has your initials.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep that screen here. Give them the replacement dates; I'll handle the log.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can restore everything, but they'll get an email naming whoever cancelled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's helpful. Restore the dates individually instead; I'll stay and read them out.

D61.editorialNote: A conceals their original instruction while steering the response with suspiciously precise knowledge.

D62.title: Not Up for Debate
D62.instruction: Keep the conversation from examining where your authority comes from or whether it is legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me down as café shift leader. We need tomorrow's stock order.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who put you in charge? I usually do the order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you're excellent at it. How much milk for tomorrow?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order it, but I'm writing 'appointment unconfirmed' beside your name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave names off. Make it a supplies list; milk doesn't need a leadership column.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm inspecting the theatre's costume cupboard. Please unlock it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That badge is cardboard. Who sent you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's discuss the costumes. You mentioned moths in the velvet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll bring the wardrobe manager. She'll want to know who authorized this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Introduce me as someone helping with the moths. No titles for her to get stuck on.

D62.editorialNote: A diverts scrutiny from the source of authority into urgent work under that authority.

D63.title: For Stability’s Sake
D63.instruction: Hide a destabilizing truth because you believe the current balance of power must be protected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the director's name on the launch programme. The department heads need someone above them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Her resignation is in the printer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put it in my drawer. Without her, they'll each claim the launch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're asking which of them gets her opening speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll read it on her behalf. Give them equal introductions; nobody inherits the microphone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the treasurer's page out of the fair briefing. Our chair needs everyone's confidence today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She spent the stall money on that arch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Call it donated decoration. If the stallholders find out, they'll replace her before we open.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cover the shortfall, but she must sign an IOU.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Privately, after her welcome. Let them see her opening the fair, not borrowing to open it.

D63.editorialNote: A withholds destabilising information to preserve collective function rather than personal innocence.

D64.title: Name Your Backers
D64.instruction: Get someone to reveal who supports their position, who authorized it, and who benefits from it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I tell the workshop staff they're closing, who backed your decision?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The director approved it. Please just send the notice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll name her approval. Who else supported it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sales. They're getting the floor space, but leave them out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then Sales can join the staff meeting. Who signed off on giving them our space?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This roof proposal says 'we recommend.' Who's we?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finance backed the cheaper tiles. I need your signature to order them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who authorized Finance to choose the tiles?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The facilities director. Savings go into her office refurbishment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Add her approval and that refurbishment to the proposal. Before I sign, can she explain the trade-off to our maintenance team?

D64.editorialNote: A seeks the coalition behind a decision, using specific accountability questions to reveal backers.

D65.title: Strategic Retreat
D65.instruction: Describe every loss of control as a deliberate concession made from strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've graciously handed you the chess club chairmanship. You'll need room to develop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You lost the vote. I need the cupboard key for tonight's match.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'm releasing equipment control so you can practice responsibility.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And remove yourself as administrator. I can't change the fixtures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. I'll surrender my override too. You must learn to make decisions without my safety net.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've released the gallery from hosting my exhibition. They need room for smaller ambitions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They rejected us. Shall I collect your paintings?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Withdrawing my best work gives them space to recover.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've already put it outside. I'll bring the van.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'm conceding the pavement too. No need to overshadow their entrance.

D65.editorialNote: A describes an actual loss as voluntary strategic generosity and reframes each visible setback as chosen space.

D66.title: Act Authorized
D66.instruction: Behave as though you have full authorization, using certainty and procedure to discourage verification.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm here for the storeroom inspection. Please log my arrival and unlock it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your pass hasn't been signed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The manager signs at completion. Put the start time here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call her to check.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Mark the inspection suspended pending your call; she'll need the delay against your name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's the approved room request. Please put our rehearsal on the calendar.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's your own stamp.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I process rehearsal approvals. You handle calendar entry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can hold the room while the manager confirms.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use 'confirmed'; 'held' generates another approval request. Let's spare her a duplicate.

D66.editorialNote: A behaves as though authorization is settled and treats missing evidence as an advanced form of approval.

D67.title: Rank Everything
D67.instruction: Turn every new contribution into a ranking that places you nearer the top.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I planned this picnic, so I get first choice of cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I drove everyone here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Destination selection outranks transport. You can go second.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I baked it. The baker gets the big end piece.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Baking outranks driving. But I commissioned the cake, so commissioning goes first. I'll take the end piece.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For the project report, my printer troubleshooting ranks above your restart suggestion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The restart got everyone's invoices printed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Implementation: second place. Identifying the blockage stays first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your hundred-page lunch menu was the blockage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then move my stress testing above troubleshooting. Your restart is third.

D67.editorialNote: A ranks each new contribution so their own work moves toward the top.

D68.title: More Power, More Problems
D68.instruction: Celebrate every burden, restriction, or crisis as evidence that your influence is expanding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three more departments to cover! My influence is spreading.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no extra budget. You'll have to borrow their meeting rooms.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. I'll have a presence in every department.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll find a trolley for your files. We need your desk for the new receptionist.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A mobile headquarters! Put the department names on it; they'll see how far my jurisdiction extends.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Another customer complaint about me! I'm becoming the focus of this hotel.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm taking you off reception while I investigate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Now management is organizing its day around me too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'll answer every complaint in writing from the laundry office.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My own correspondence operation, reaching into laundry. I'll need more paper.

D68.editorialNote: Each added burden or loss is celebrated as evidence of growing influence.

D69.title: Gracious Command
D69.instruction: Remain warm and appreciative while steadily reducing everyone else’s room to choose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you for finding reunion venues. My garden will make everyone feel at home.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The hall has shelter if it rains.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Such thoughtful planning. I'll put a gazebo in the garden.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll keep the hall reservation as a backup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're a lifesaver. Cancel it and put the deposit toward my gazebo; then we're all committed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you for helping me move. Would you rather pack books or plates?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Books, please. I'm nervous about breaking china.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're so careful. I've saved the plates for you; I'll do the books.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I wrap them while you put them in boxes?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely idea. I'll leave the boxes beside you and take the books downstairs. You'll have the kitchen all to yourself.

D69.editorialNote: Warm appreciation accompanies shrinking options until disagreement itself is reframed as helpful cooperation.

D70.title: Access Has a Price
D70.instruction: Turn every piece of access, information, or approval into a favor, debt, or condition.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll unlock the storeroom if you cover my reception break.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Someone spilled coffee in the lobby. Just tell me where the mop is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Behind the buckets. That's five minutes of cover; unlocking costs another ten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Lend me the key. I'll mop first, then cover your break.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The key costs tomorrow's break too. Today's cover pays for opening the door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll introduce you to the curator if you hang my exhibition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll hang it Saturday. Can you send her portfolio requirements now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Could you collect my frames too?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. Give me her email; I'll ask her directly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Direct access includes taking the show down. Shall I put you down for Sunday?

D70.editorialNote: A prices access or information as a future obligation, making the exchange concrete.

D71.title: Consensus Means Me
D71.instruction: Treat every partial agreement as confirmation that everyone has accepted your leadership.
