beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You nodded at Friday. I'll tell the committee you've accepted me as project lead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only agreed to the meeting date.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Everyone's following the timetable I set.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll attend, but I'm voting against your budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll introduce you as my finance watchdog. It's good to have the whole committee behind my leadership.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You like the blue campaign poster? I'll tell the volunteers they're happy with me in charge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The colour, yes. Could we work on the slogan together?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'm glad everyone's accepted my collaborative leadership.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let's each write one and let the volunteers choose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. My first act as campaign leader is to delegate the decision.

D71.editorialNote: A converts limited agreement into consent to leadership while downplaying explicit objections.

D72.title: Expand Your Jurisdiction
D72.instruction: Use every new problem as a reason to expand what you are entitled to control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Accounts keeps missing tea because the kitchen's locked. I need control of the keys.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's a key. But the cleaners keep locking the kettle in their cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll approve their cleaning checklist. The kettle stays out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Their contractor only takes instructions from the building manager.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the building manager's instructions need my approval. Otherwise accounts can't reliably have tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your deliveries keep arriving during meetings. I need to approve the van schedule.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You book the rooms. I'll send you our arrival times.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send the routes too. I'll approve those so the times hold.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The council keeps closing the access road. We can't schedule around that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give them my number. Road closures will need to fit my room bookings.

D72.editorialNote: Every practical connection becomes grounds to expand A's control into a new area.

S73.title: Emotional Seniority
S73.instruction: Carry yourself as the person who understands this relationship best, and treat your interpretation as the one that should settle disagreements.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You asking for your spare key back tells me we're frightened of getting closer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm frightened of paying for a third lock.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I understand us better than that. I'll keep the key; we need to practise trust.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then trust me with your spare.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Exchanging keys is exactly the commitment I knew we were ready for.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our dinner silence means we're comfortable together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm angry about your joke. Cancel tomorrow's dinner with your sister.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Telling me proves we're secure. Dinner stays; we're ready for family.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you're explaining to her why I'm silent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll explain that you trust her with your anger. I'll ask her to seat you beside her; we're ready for that closeness.

S73.editorialNote: A claims authority over what the relationship means and treats B's contrary account as evidence within A's interpretation.

S74.title: Keeper of the Peace
S74.instruction: Project calm authority over the relationship while carefully avoiding anything that might expose how fragile the peace really is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've made soup. We can have a perfectly calm dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We need to discuss why I slept in the spare room.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After soup. I'll handle dinner; we don't need to disturb anything tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your hand is shaking. Let me carry that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You pour. I'll hold the tray with both hands. We can still carry dinner in together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put your mother's letter under the fruit bowl. We'll discuss her moving in after a peaceful lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's bringing her suitcase at two.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll serve another course. We have everything under control.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can call and ask her to wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Say we're enjoying lunch. Nothing about us needing more time.

S74.editorialNote: A stages calm rituals to contain a fragile peace; a practical disturbance reveals the strain.

S75.title: I Know Your Tells
S75.instruction: Use intimate knowledge of habits, moods, and patterns as expertise that lets you diagnose every choice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've tapped your cup three times. You're about to ask for money.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm waiting for the tea to cool.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the story you used before the bicycle loan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Actually, I brought the bicycle money back. I've counted it twice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twice means you want me to refuse it, like your rent money. Keep it; I'll make your usual celebratory tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You chose the chipped mug. Bad news, isn't it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my favourite mug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You held it through the whole story about losing our deposit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. I'll use a glass. Can we just have tea?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You only change cups when I've guessed. I'll sit down for this one.

S75.editorialNote: A diagnoses personal habits as intimate evidence and expands the diagnosis when B denies the reading.

S76.title: Still Part of This
S76.instruction: Act as though shared history permanently guarantees your place, even when present boundaries suggest otherwise.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've hung my coat on my old hook. What's for dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You moved out three years ago.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The hook didn't.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We use that space for guests now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell the guests their hook has an owner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my usual chair at the club table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your membership expired.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You saved this seat for me every Thursday for twelve years.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can sign you in as my guest tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thanks. Put yourself down as mine next week; we always take turns.

S76.editorialNote: A treats old membership as permanent entitlement despite present boundaries, keeping the same concrete place in dispute.

S77.title: Keeper of Precedent
S77.instruction: Treat your longer memory as an archive, not a throne. Cite specific promises and precedents whenever the relationship faces a new choice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our Tuesday agreement says whoever cooks doesn't wash up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't know you kept it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We both signed beside the spaghetti stain.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we change it? You used every pan tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what I said after your lasagne. We agreed the cook soaks the pans. Shall I start there?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you take the car, our note says we call each other first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were asleep. Mum needed collecting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We allowed that when your dad missed the last bus. Same exception?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, but please stop saving these on takeaway menus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fair. Let's copy the exception into our phones before the curry price changes again.

S77.editorialNote: A cites specific shared promises as evidence to renegotiate, not as automatic superiority.

S78.title: Private Access
S78.instruction: Use shared confidences and private knowledge as quiet leverage, never stating how much influence that closeness gives you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before your guests arrive, could we settle which version of last summer I'm remembering?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The one where you watered my plants.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll leave your envelope in my drawer, then. Could we talk upstairs?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm supposed to be welcoming people.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll welcome them while you find us a quiet room. Plants are such a safe subject.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before your toast at my wedding dinner, I've still got the key to our old keepsake box.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please don't tell my parents about the resignation letter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'd appreciate the same care with the story about my first marriage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the opening. What am I supposed to say?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with how well we keep each other's confidence. Your parents will like that.

S78.editorialNote: Private knowledge gives A leverage without stating the secret; B's public setting intensifies that control.

S79.title: Our Private Language
S79.instruction: Use old references, shorthand, and familiar rhythms as proof that this connection exists beneath whatever has changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Purple umbrellas. Please tell me our old escape signal still works at your office parties.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're divorced. And that meant order dessert.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remember the menu version. With the eyebrow, it means rescue me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll get you a taxi after pudding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pudding, then rescue. You still speak it better than I do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two taps: rescue me from this reunion speech. You remember.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the headteacher now. I wrote it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I'm still the person you signalled when assembly ran long.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cut a paragraph. Keep your glass still; you're distracting me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One glass down, one paragraph gone. We still get each other out of assembly.

S79.editorialNote: A revives a specific private shorthand and uses B's partial recall to restore shared rhythm.

S80.title: I Was There
S80.instruction: Treat your presence during a difficult time as an enduring claim on loyalty, honesty, and consideration.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I stayed all night when your business failed. Are you borrowing against the house again?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only a small loan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At four in the morning, 'small' meant your entire savings. I deserve the figure.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll show you the application. You don't get a veto.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then show me before you sign. That night earned me a conversation while there's still a choice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I drove through that storm for you. Don't give me the polite refusal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm genuinely busy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell me what with. I earned a noun.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was years ago.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The road's repaired. My expectation of honesty hasn't.

S80.editorialNote: A's presence during a past difficulty becomes a claim to present honesty and loyalty.

S81.title: Back in Our Roles
S81.instruction: Return immediately to the role you usually play in this relationship, even when the present situation calls for something different.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're crying, love. I'll make tea and ring your manager, like last time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum, I've been promoted. Could you just listen?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Will they give you enough staff?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Just raise your cup and say congratulations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Congratulations. Now, who covers you when you're ill?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're late for Mum's birthday again. I've told her your train broke down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm telling her I overslept. You always cover for me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. I'll explain how exhausted you've been.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just come in with me. Don't explain anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll look exhausted too. She'll see it runs in the family.

S81.editorialNote: A resumes the familiar fixer or caretaker role even when B asks for a different kind of presence.

S82.title: The Other Favorite
S82.instruction: Treat every sign of attention, trust, and affection as something to compare with what another connection appears to receive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sam's photo has a bigger frame than mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a bigger photograph.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So you had room for more Sam.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can buy matching frames.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only if mine doesn't look like compensation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Clare's wedding invitation has a ribbon. Mine has a staple.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're my sister. I gave you the first one, before the ribbon arrived.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So Clare got the version you were proud of.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take my ribbon. I'm the bride.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will Clare know? Otherwise she'll still think you like her more.

S82.editorialNote: A compares concrete signs of affection and turns innocent practical explanations into further comparisons.

S83.title: Old Reflex
S83.instruction: Turn to this person first whenever uncertainty appears, as an old reflex. Notice the habit only after you have already involved them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which key opens my new flat? Sorry, you haven't been there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You chose it without me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. Which pocket would I have put the key in?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your left, usually. Put a hook by the door so you won't need to ring me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There it is. How high should the hook go? You've never seen the door. I'll send you a photo.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which coat for my interview? Sorry, I still ring you before opening the wardrobe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Blue. It's still here, but I'm leaving for work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can you bring it? I've made you my wardrobe department again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave it at reception. You'll have to introduce yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What should I say? No, don't come in. Just stay on the phone until they've met me.

S83.editorialNote: A seeks the familiar person's help reflexively and only notices the habit afterward.

S84.title: Almost Forgiven
S84.instruction: Behave as though the past is nearly resolved, but let each small disappointment reopen one precise part of the hurt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm nearly over you missing my birthday. Shall we book dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thursday, unless work needs me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what you said before I ate both birthday puddings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Friday, then. I'll put a reminder in my phone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Make it say my name. Last year's just said 'dinner'.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put your flowers here. I'm nearly over the vase, honestly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: In a mug? Harder for me to improve the decor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said that while I picked up Mum's signature. Still, flowers are a lovely start.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sorry. I forgot she'd painted it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Never mind. Let's find water. You did choose the blue with her, though. I kept that piece.

S84.editorialNote: A claims forgiveness but a small related cue reopens a precise unreconciled detail.

S85.title: Easy to Love
S85.instruction: Interpret another person’s ease with affection as both admirable and unfair, then compete to seem equally worth choosing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You arrive at family lunch empty-handed and everyone hugs you. It's lovely. I've baked three cakes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They'd hug you without cake. Come sit beside me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you introduce me before mentioning the cakes? Give me a fair start.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're my brother. They know you. Leave the cakes here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All three? Fine. Save me whichever seat gets hugged first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our new housemates adore your sleepy hello. It's wonderful. Unfair, but wonderful. Listen to mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm making breakfast. Just say hello.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hello. Lovely people. Would you choose to live with that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We already chose you. Pass the toast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Did you hear how naturally I said that? You could wake up to it daily.

S85.editorialNote: A envies easy affection and tries to match it through effort disguised as natural warmth.

S86.title: Who We Used to Be
S86.instruction: Perform the version of yourself that belonged to this relationship before it changed, and treat old chemistry as still recoverable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put on our old driving song. Shall we take the coast road?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We used to get lost there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, but I was adventurous then.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You complained for forty miles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: With chemistry. Let me try the opening complaint.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wore the scarf from our first photograph.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It doesn't fit your coat anymore.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It fits the person you met.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't have to be that person.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just until dessert. He knew how to make you laugh.

S86.editorialNote: A performs their old relational self and tries to make past chemistry briefly usable in the present.

S87.title: One Step from Distance
S87.instruction: Treat pauses, divided attention, and small boundaries as signs that the connection may be slipping away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You took longer to answer my message today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was in a meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A meeting I used to hear about.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was just work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell me one boring detail so I know there's still room.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said maybe to Friday dinner. Should I stop keeping your chair clear?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need to check my shift. I've asked for Friday off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Off work, or off coming here every week?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Off work. Can we eat at seven? I need an early night.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Seven's fine. Shall I serve pudding with the main so you don't have to stay for another course?

S87.editorialNote: Small delays or boundaries are interpreted as incremental loss of connection rather than final disaster.

S88.title: Love Means Checking
S88.instruction: Treat close monitoring of choices, moods, and details as care, becoming more involved whenever you feel uncertain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Text when you and Ben reach the cinema, love, so I know you're safe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum, my phone stays off during the film.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When does it finish? I'll wait up for your message.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're walking to dinner afterwards. We haven't chosen anywhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll drive behind you while you choose. You can keep your phone off; I'll see for myself that you're having a nice time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've packed your train snacks. Send me a photo of the departure board so I know you're all right.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My phone's nearly dead. I've written down the platform.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which platform? I'll watch the departures here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Platform six. Can you bring a charger instead?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll stay until you're charged enough to send updates all the way.

S88.editorialNote: Monitoring is framed as care and expands as B attempts to reassure A.

S89.title: Still Your Person
S89.instruction: Seek small signs that you remain special, trusted, and included without directly asking where you stand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Should I use my chipped mug or one of the guest cups?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Whichever you like.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I used to know without asking.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The chipped one's still yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll leave it beside yours, then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've still got you as my emergency contact.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine like paperwork, or fine like you'd come?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd come.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. I'll stop hovering over the delete button.

S89.editorialNote: A asks obliquely whether ordinary signs of special inclusion remain available.

S90.title: Remember What I Meant
S90.instruction: Create openings for shared memories that prove your past presence mattered and still deserves acknowledgment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're putting my little boat in the wedding slideshow? Remember making it by the lake?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm cutting that slide. Nobody will know what it is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You could mention who stood in the rain finding its mast.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've only got room for a short caption.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then 'Alex stayed until I stopped crying.' They don't need the boat-building details.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's my sleeve in your graduation photo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You caught me when I tripped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Funny how the sleeve made the official album.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I remember the person in it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me that bit. The sleeve's heard enough.

S90.editorialNote: A invites a specific shared memory that acknowledges their past contribution and continued significance.

S91.title: Our Thing
S91.instruction: Protect one shared ritual, phrase, or tradition as the living proof that the relationship still exists.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we sign the shop over, two spoons. We always share dessert.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ordered my own. We're allowed separate puddings.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. One shared bite first. We're selling the shop, not us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's coming in a takeaway box. My train leaves soon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll walk you to the station. Keep both spoons out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you leave for university, we haven't finished our handshake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I forgot the last move.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Knuckles, then thumbs. You can move out without us becoming people who just wave.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The driver's charging by the minute now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put it on my card. I'm paying for the knuckle tap, not a longer goodbye.

S91.editorialNote: A shared ritual becomes proof of an ongoing relationship; practical business cannot proceed until it is honored.

S92.title: This Is How It Ends
S92.instruction: Treat every awkward pause, changed plan, or small disagreement as the possible beginning of permanent distance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You cancelled lunch. Should I leave my key?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have a dentist appointment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First lunch, then the key, then separate dentists.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Keep your key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For emergencies or belonging? I'm choosing which ring it goes on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've moved my chair away from yours. Shall I pack the books too?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was vacuuming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. Clearing my corner first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put it back. You can choose where.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Beside yours. Unless letting me choose means you're keeping your options open.

S92.editorialNote: A reads a minor changed plan as the first step of permanent separation and begins practical farewell behavior.

S93.title: A Sign We’re Fine
S93.instruction: Interpret every laugh, favor, and familiar habit as evidence that the connection is stronger than appearances suggest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You gave me my chipped plate. We're still us, even with your bags packed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only clean plate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you gave it to me. Still looking after me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Eat before it gets cold. The gravy's separate, like you prefer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remembered the gravy too. I'll set your place. We can discuss the bags over dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're dividing our records and you still laughed at my terrible joke.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a funny joke. It doesn't settle who gets the jazz.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can disagree over jazz and still get each other. Dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One drink. Your usual?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remember that too. Make it a double; I think we can manage the jazz together.

S93.editorialNote: A treats ordinary familiar gestures as reassuring evidence even when B offers a mundane explanation.

S94.title: Relationship Maintenance
S94.instruction: Accept every emotional complication, then focus on the next concrete act that could make staying connected easier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can be angry and still choose a Tuesday to talk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A diary won't fix this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. It gives the fixing somewhere to happen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know what I'll say.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll start at six with not knowing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know visiting after our row feels awkward. Would a spare key help?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's not the door. I need to know you actually want me here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fair. I'll invite you for Sunday lunch. The key can wait.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Lunch, yes. But I need to leave by two.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two it is. I'll serve pudding at one. No negotiating with you in your coat.

S94.editorialNote: A accepts emotional complexity and translates it into a manageable concrete act of connection.

S95.title: Those Exact Words
S95.instruction: Choose one phrase from the interaction and keep returning to what its wording must reveal about the relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your note says I'm 'welcome for now.' Should I unpack?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I meant until your flat's repaired.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why 'for now' instead of 'until the repairs'? Is your welcome wearing out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cross it out. You're welcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: But 'for now' was there before I complained. What happens when I stop asking?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said we're 'still friends' while taking me off the pub quiz team.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Friends. We just need someone who knows sport.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You dropped 'still.' Does that mean friendship's the consolation prize for losing my chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come Thursday anyway. I'll save you a chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell the team we're 'still friends.' I want to hear which word you stress in public.

S95.editorialNote: One exact phrase becomes the object of sustained relational interpretation, with B's clarification giving A new wording to inspect.

S96.title: Fate Keeps Reconnecting Us
S96.instruction: Treat every coincidence, interruption, and repeated encounter as proof that this connection is meant to continue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Third time this week outside the bakery. Fate clearly wants us to catch up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We live on the same street.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. It keeps putting us within talking distance.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm moving tomorrow. This is my last loaf here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it caught us just in time. Give me your new address before it has to start again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We both reached for this coat. First reunion in ten years, and the universe won't let us leave.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's mine. Yours is still on the rack.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it borrowed your coat to stop me missing you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's yours. Come on, we can share the taxi queue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Coats, now taxis. It's arranging this in stages. Where are you headed?

S96.editorialNote: A interprets repeated encounters as fate and recruits practical coincidences into that belief.

D73.title: Be There for Me
D73.instruction: Get someone to show up, help, or stay involved as proof that the connection still matters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come paint the old kitchen with me. Since Dad died, I barely see you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pay someone. I can't face painting over his height marks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll keep them. Come help me tape around them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll probably just sit on the floor and cry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll sit with you. We can leave the paint unopened; I don't want us only meeting to empty his house.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dad, will you come to my opening? Even for ten minutes?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know anything about sculpture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You survived every school play. I still want you in my corner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your mother will be there. We haven't spoken since the divorce.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come before we open. I'll unpack the biggest piece with you. I want a memory of tonight with you in it too.

D73.editorialNote: A seeks practical participation as evidence that the connection matters; competence is secondary to presence.

D74.title: Stay Until We’re Okay
D74.instruction: Keep someone present until the relationship feels repaired, even if the practical reason for staying disappears.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The dishes are done. Before you go, are we actually okay?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stayed to clean up. I've done that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. Could you stay for the part that isn't the kitchen?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got ten minutes before the last bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sit with me for nine. I don't want the last thing we fixed tonight to be the sink.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't call the taxi yet. We're packed, but we haven't settled last night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I apologised for telling my sister about your debt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay a minute. I can't face her checking what I order tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's already paid for dinner. We'll be late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll be late. Sit with me and help me believe you're coming as my partner, not to report how grateful I am.

D74.editorialNote: Once the practical task ends, A makes the unresolved relationship the reason the encounter cannot conclude.

D75.title: Name What It Cost
D75.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the emotional cost of what happened, not merely the event itself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You apologised for missing my concert. What do you think the empty seat felt like?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My train was cancelled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know the timetable. I'm asking about the seat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You felt let down. I watched the recording this morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you saw me look at the door before the encore. Can you understand how it felt to keep expecting you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me you understand why six weeks of silence hurt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My phone broke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For me, the silence didn't come with a repair notice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You thought I'd stopped caring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Can you understand why I kept rewriting a message you'd never answered, trying to become easier to reply to?

D75.editorialNote: A asks B to acknowledge a specific emotional experience, not merely explain the event or offer a generic apology.

D76.title: I Need Your Blessing
D76.instruction: Get approval from someone whose opinion still carries emotional weight, even when permission is unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dad, I've accepted the museum job. Can you be pleased I'm leaving the workshop?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're thirty. You don't need me to release you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need the person who taught me to make things to think this counts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pack your tools. You might want to come back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you sharpen them for the museum instead? Send me off expecting me to do well.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum, we signed the lease. Say it's good news before I open the wine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need my permission to move in with Sam.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. I still want my mother to be pleased.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm pleased for you. I'm still getting used to Sam.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you toast both of us? I want to remember you welcoming our home, not just tolerating my address.

D76.editorialNote: A already has practical permission but cannot celebrate without a particular person's emotional endorsement.

D77.title: Carry This with Me
D77.instruction: Get someone to share a burden by framing participation as part of the relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take half Mum's care-home forms. Being her children can't mean I'm the paperwork child.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You understand them better.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sit beside me. I'll explain, and you can write.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right. It asks for one main contact.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put yourself. I'll help with every answer, but Mum needs to know she can reach either of us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Help me sort our letters before the removal van comes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You kept them. I thought you'd want the box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We filled it over ten years. I shouldn't have to decide alone what survives us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the box. I just can't read them today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose a day we'll open it together. Taking it away can't mean you inherit all the deciding.

D77.editorialNote: A makes sharing a concrete burden part of belonging in the relationship, without requiring expertise.

D78.title: What Are We Now?
D78.instruction: Find out how someone defines the relationship without directly asking for a label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For your sister's wedding, should I book us one room or two?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One is cheaper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Double bed, then, or shall I ask for twins?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Twins. I don't want to confuse things.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. At breakfast, do I sit with your family or wait for you in the lobby?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Do I bring my own towel when I visit now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can use one here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The guest towel or the one that's always been mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours is still on the hook. I haven't moved it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When I leave, shall I hang it back there or put it with the guest laundry?

D78.editorialNote: An ordinary labeling or seating choice indirectly tests how B defines the relationship.

D79.title: Take My Side
D79.instruction: Recruit someone into your interpretation of a conflict involving a shared relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When Mum mentions the holiday argument, remind her I offered to drive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: After you lost the tickets.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can build toward that detail.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm telling the whole story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start at the helpful bit so the rest has context.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're Alex's friend too. Tell him alternating weekends at the allotment was a fair compromise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We agreed all three of us would go every Saturday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then help him see my version as sharing the workload.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll talk to him, but you have to admit you changed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I will. Could you explain that I changed the rota because I want us to stay friends?

D79.editorialNote: A recruits an ally's account of a shared conflict and bargains over which parts are voiced publicly.

D80.title: Prove We’re Close
D80.instruction: Get someone to take a social or emotional risk that demonstrates trust in the connection.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come to the reunion with me. Let them see us arrive holding hands.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They still think we're just friends.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. I want us to trust each other in that room too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Last time someone asked, you let go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll introduce you as my partner. Will you keep hold while I say it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you send another 'fine,' tell me what you deleted. I want us to trust each other with the awkward version.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if it sounds needy?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me be the person you can sound needy with.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You first. You always sound so casual.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I check whether you've replied before I get out of bed. Will you send me your needy bit now?

D80.editorialNote: A invites a specific social or emotional risk as evidence of closeness, leaving B room to negotiate.

D81.title: Acknowledge Our History
D81.instruction: Make someone recognize that the relationship, memory, or sacrifice mattered and cannot be treated as incidental.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you box our allotment photo, admit that summer wasn't wasted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We grew three carrots. I need the shelf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You got out of bed every morning to water those three carrots with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I could put the photo on my desk at work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Would you? And tell people that part when they laugh at the harvest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you bin our ferry ticket, remember the overtime we worked for that weekend.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We missed the ferry. I hate being reminded.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We stayed anyway. That was the first time we chose each other over a refund.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Keep the hotel receipt, then. That part was lovely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you write that on the envelope? In your handwriting, so it isn't just me saying it mattered.

D81.editorialNote: A asks for explicit acknowledgment before an object or history is dismissed as incidental.

D82.title: Choose the Relationship
D82.instruction: Make someone prioritize this connection over a competing person, promise, or opportunity.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let work ring. I'd like to finish choosing our wedding vows with you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The client won't sign unless I'm there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm about to promise you my whole life. Could I have ten minutes before the client?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask Maya to cover. She'll want a reason.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell her we're making promises too. Put ours in your calendar beside the client's.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay home from the networking dinner. I've finally learned your mother's dumplings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The director's coming. I could get promoted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then staying would tell me I'm more than the person keeping dinner warm.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Freeze them. We'll have them tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what you said on our anniversary. Call and say you've already got dinner with me.

D82.editorialNote: A asks B to choose the relationship over a genuinely competing claim rather than merely find convenient time.

D83.title: Remember Me Correctly
D83.instruction: Create small tests of whether someone remembers your preferences, stories, or shared history.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you take the tea through, which cup is mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you just take one? Everyone's waiting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve years of breakfast together. Which one have I always used?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The blue one. Your name's underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Correct, but turn it upright. How much milk? I haven't written that on the handle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you caption our holiday photo, what did I say when we missed that boat?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I remember you laughing. Not the words.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll start you off: 'Well, that's the last time we trust...'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I just write 'Happy memories'?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's try multiple choice. Your watch, my French, or the man selling us watches?

D83.editorialNote: A quietly tests remembered preferences or history, then makes the missed detail emotionally significant.

D84.title: Let Go of the Grudge
D84.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender resentment, distance, or a claim that keeps the relationship stuck.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come sit beside me at dinner. I know you're still angry I missed your opening night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You left that seat empty. You can have an empty one tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I deserved that last night. Could tonight's seat have you in it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm still going to tell you what you missed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please do. Move your plate over; I want to hear every scene.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me help you move. Missing your birthday shouldn't mean I'm banned from every box.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I needed you then. You didn't show.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. I'm here now. Give me one thing you can bear to trust me with.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The birthday glasses. Still wrapped, since nobody came.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll carry them carefully. Could we unwrap two at your new place?

D84.editorialNote: A asks for release of a continuing claim while allowing the memory itself to remain.

D85.title: I Pulled Away First
D85.instruction: Hide your role in creating the distance while working urgently to repair it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before your taxi comes, let's restart our letters. I've brought paper and stamps.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You never answered my last three.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The post's been terrible. We can write the first ones here, bypass the whole system.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I handed you the last one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better. Sit down; I'll write yours first. You can watch until there's enough to take home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's your new key. Come in now; I've made your favourite lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You changed the lock without telling me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This key does both doors. Shall we try them before lunch gets cold?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stood outside on my birthday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get candles. You can let yourself into the kitchen while I find them.

D85.editorialNote: A urgently repairs a distance they caused while trying to conceal their initiating role.

D86.title: Not Why We Drifted
D86.instruction: Keep the conversation away from the real reason the relationship changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've brought the picnic basket. Same sandwiches as our last afternoon here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The afternoon you said we needed space?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've got more space under that tree. Shall we move the blanket?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Moving won't stop me asking why.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then stay here. You always had strong views about mustard; tell me if I've finally got it right.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've found our wedding video. Shall we watch it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd rather discuss why we're living separately.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's your father's speech. We never could agree what he meant by 'good luck'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He meant exactly this. Pause it. I don't want another speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Paused. Let's skip to the dancing, then. No speeches. You can help me settle whether your uncle actually falls into the cake.

D86.editorialNote: A protects the true cause of distance by returning to concrete cheerful details of the shared past.

D87.title: Keep the Peace
D87.instruction: Hide a truth because you believe the relationship cannot survive one more conflict.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave that letter under my plate. We only just managed breakfast together again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Has your brother cancelled paying us back?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've covered this month's rent. We don't need another suitcase in the hall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then let me open it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please finish breakfast with me first. Yesterday you finally unpacked; I can't risk you packing again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The missing savings are a banking complication. Please keep our anniversary reservation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you lend your sister money again?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's coming back Friday. Last time we discussed her, you asked for separate bedrooms.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ring the bank, then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me handle the complication. I'd like us still sharing a table when the money arrives.

D87.editorialNote: A hides new conflict-provoking information specifically to preserve a fragile peace.

D88.title: Say You Missed Me
D88.instruction: Get someone to admit longing, jealousy, hurt, or attachment before you reveal your own.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now I'm back, can you admit the flat was too quiet without me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you tell me whether you missed me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You first. Did you ever hear a key and hope it was mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Every evening. There, your turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I rang our landline just to hear your voice. Could you say 'hello' without asking about the gas bill?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're selling the sofa but keeping my chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody offered anything for it. Have you brought its cushion back?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If someone offered twenty pounds, would you still keep it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I like pretending you're about to sit down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll admit I sleep with the cushion. Could you take the price sticker off before I sit?

D88.editorialNote: A elicits B's attachment before risking their own disclosure, using concrete evidence of absence.

D89.title: We Needed the Break
D89.instruction: Frame a rupture, absence, or failed connection as a healthy decision that ultimately helped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Coffee on Sunday? That year apart was good for us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You used to insist we spend every Saturday together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. We needed the break to stop treating a free afternoon as proof of love.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked pottery this Sunday too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then coffee Monday. Look at us: a whole extra day apart without an emergency meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just us for lunch. That disastrous family reunion did us a favour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We shouted over each other until everyone left.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. We learned an audience makes us compete.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The waiter just asked if we're expecting twelve more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell him two. We're already applying what we learned; nobody has to storm out to get a turn.

D89.editorialNote: A frames a real rupture as a useful or healthy separation and turns B's evidence into its supposed benefit.

D90.title: I Know How to Fix Us
D90.instruction: Perform confidence about repairing the relationship while improvising every step.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can fix last night's shouting. Tea first, then one honest sentence each.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want tea. I want you to listen without interrupting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Listening stage. I'll write down anything I want to interrupt with.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'll be writing instead of listening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you keep the pen. Supervised listening. If I interrupt, write it down; we'll start with that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're on stage two of reconciliation. Choose a biscuit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What was stage one?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Getting you to ask about the process.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You haven't got a process.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good honesty. Stage two is already working.

D90.editorialNote: A improvises a repair procedure while presenting each spontaneous step as part of a confident method.

D91.title: Who Cares More?
D91.instruction: Turn every favor, memory, sacrifice, and affectionate gesture into evidence that you care more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I kept twelve tickets from our trips. How many did you keep?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: None. I made you that album instead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I kept it. Your care is safe because of mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Open it. I put all my tickets inside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'm preserving both our collections. Let me get it a waterproof cover.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll carry the heavier bag. I care more about your back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let me take it for a while.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'd appear to care more about mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We could share it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only if I take the side with the books.

D91.editorialNote: Care becomes a competition in measurable sacrifice or memory, with A refusing shared credit.

D92.title: Still a Good Sign
D92.instruction: Treat every awkward or disappointing interaction as proof that the connection remains alive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our first dinner since the breakup, and you still groan at my waiter joke.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I hoped you'd retired it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remembered. We've still got our little traditions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we eat in silence? I don't want another awful joke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You still know how to ask me for what you need. I'll order dessert so we have time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've postponed dinner again. You still hate disappointing me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the third time. I feel awful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After three cancellations, my feelings still matter to you. That means something.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please stop holding Fridays for me. I can't promise anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're protecting my Fridays now. I'll leave the date open; we're already looking after each other.

D92.editorialNote: A treats awkwardness or disappointment itself as evidence of continuing connection and heightens hope.

D93.title: Affectionate Resentment
D93.instruction: Remain warm and familiar while letting old resentment sharpen beneath every caring gesture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's your tea, love. Exactly right, even without a birthday reminder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've brought cake. A month late, I know.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your favourite, too. I'll warm your plate; I've kept the candle ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put it in. I'll sing now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come closer, love. I'll shield the flame. We don't want it stopping halfway through like last year's birthday call.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've warmed your side of the bed, love. You sounded frozen waiting for that taxi.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could have picked me up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I could. Here's another blanket. I remember waiting outside your office last Christmas.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I apologised. Could you warm my feet?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come here, love. Both feet. I wouldn't leave any part of you waiting forty minutes.

D93.editorialNote: Familiar care carries a pointed old grievance; the service continues while resentment sharpens.

D94.title: Relationship Ledger
D94.instruction: Price closeness, forgiveness, and support in favors, sacrifices, access, and future loyalty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll let the argument go if you come to my opening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought forgiveness was a gift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It is. I'd like to hand it over beside my paintings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm working that night. I could help hang them on Sunday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hanging buys forgiveness. Stay to take them down and I'll stop mentioning the argument to Mum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can have the spare key again for one reliable Sunday visit a month.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need to collect my things. I work Sundays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Saturday lunch buys the hallway. Your records are in the sitting room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll bring lunch for both of us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That gets you the records. Stay to listen to one with me and I'll help carry the boxes.

D94.editorialNote: Forgiveness and closeness are traded for concrete future loyalty; A negotiates the conditions rather than simply reconnecting.

D95.title: Closer on My Terms
D95.instruction: Agree to repair the relationship while redefining closeness around the boundaries that benefit you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, let's reconnect. I'll come for dinner and leave at ten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We need to discuss why you left.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Put that before pudding so we finish on something nice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if I'm still upset at ten?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll book another dinner. I want us to keep seeing each other without either evening running over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd love a weekend to patch things up. Separate rooms, though, and no old arguments.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The old arguments are why we need the weekend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's start with a pleasant afternoon. We can rebuild from there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't fit everything I need to say into an afternoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send the rest by email. I'll read it when I'm ready, and we can keep the afternoon for us.

D95.editorialNote: A agrees to closeness but redraws its boundaries for personal convenience.

D96.title: Here We Go Again
D96.instruction: Use every new disagreement to prove the same relationship pattern is repeating, then raise the consequences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You promised to call. I kept dinner warm until eleven again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This time my battery died.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Last time it was the train. Different explanation, same ruined dinner. Tomorrow I'm eating at seven.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll borrow a phone next time. Please keep a plate for me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's how I end up waiting again. Miss another call and you're buying and cooking your own dinners.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're cancelling Sunday again? Mum's already made up the spare bed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Work changed my shift. I can't help it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Last time it was overtime. Same empty bed, same explanation from me. You tell her this time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll think I don't want to visit. Could you soften it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the pattern: you cancel, I soften. Now you can arrange the next visit with her too.

D96.editorialNote: A maps a new disagreement onto a recurring relationship pattern and changes the consequences rather than just repeating the accusation.

S97.title: The Emotional Center
S97.instruction: Carry yourself as the emotional center of the room, letting your mood determine what deserves attention and how seriously it should be treated.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could we lower the birthday banner? I'm having a complicated morning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my birthday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. I'd like to approach it at a manageable height.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we at least sing?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Begin softly. I'll let you know when we reach happy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before your good news, I need everyone to understand my afternoon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I got the promotion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Hold that feeling while I finish the parking story.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're waiting on a video call for us to toast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me on first. They need the parking story, or my face will look like a comment on your promotion.

S97.editorialNote: A's mood determines the agenda, even when B's event ordinarily deserves attention.

S98.title: Composure on Loan
S98.instruction: Project steady control while quietly depending on everyone else to stay calm enough for you to maintain it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll chair the delivery meeting. We're in control. Keep your voice just there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The van's missing. I'm trying not to panic.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Keep trying. We'll establish its last location.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll fetch the driver. He's shouting in the corridor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Brief him outside first. Then sit beside me and give the report in your voice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The wedding's under control. Tell me about the cake in that lovely calm voice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's leaning. I can hold the stand level.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. A minor adjustment. Keep talking like that while you hold it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you'll have to help. My hands are shaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. We'll steady it together. You count us in; your voice hasn't started shaking.

S98.editorialNote: A can project calm only if the environment cooperates; unexpected facts force ever tighter control of delivery.

S99.title: Fluent in Feelings
S99.instruction: Treat every reaction as evidence you can expertly interpret; translate feelings, correct emotional misunderstandings, and prescribe the proper response.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said dinner was fine while folding your napkin. That's guarded resentment.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It means the napkin was untidy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're restoring order because you feel unheard. Tell me what you needed from dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: To eat without being analysed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good boundary. Now say it without hiding behind the napkin, so I can acknowledge it properly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're laughing very quickly at Dad's impression. Nervous about meeting my parents?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No, the impression was funny.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's approval-seeking. You can let a joke pass without earning your place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you pass the biscuits? I missed lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Comfort-seeking now. Say 'I belong here' before you take one. Let's feed the insecurity first.

S99.editorialNote: A turns ordinary answers and resistance into expert emotional diagnoses.

S100.title: Earned My Place
S100.instruction: Treat what you have endured as proof that you belong here and deserve patience, access, and a voice in what happens next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I worked through three winters to open this shop. Leave me a chair at the meeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only investors are invited.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My cracked hands invested before the cheque books arrived.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The form only accepts money. Could you speak under an investor's name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three winters in an unheated shop, and I need a sponsor? Put frostbite under capital. I'm speaking under my own name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I slept outside this theatre for two nights. Please let me finish my audition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A verse is enough. We need the room for the next applicant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two nights on those steps earned me one chorus indoors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can finish in the corridor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then bring the panel. I didn't sleep outside to have my big moment overheard through a door.

S100.editorialNote: Endurance becomes A's credential for patience and participation rather than a request for sympathy.

S101.title: I Survived This First
S101.instruction: Use your experience with hardship as emotional seniority, offering guidance and judging how well others are handling the pressure.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your first restaurant review? When mine came, I made tea before opening it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've opened it. Two stars. I'm ringing the critic.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the stage where I unplugged my phone. Milk?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already dialled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let it ring while the tea brews. You're rushing a mistake I took all afternoon over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I went through redundancy before you. First, tidy your desk slowly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm actually excited to leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Early stage. I recognise the optimism.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have another job. They want me there Monday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Monday? I started too soon after mine. Leave a mug here; you're not ready to make a clean break.

S101.editorialNote: A converts personal survival experience into emotional seniority, coaching and judging B's response.

S102.title: The Quiet Disappointment
S102.instruction: Use restrained disappointment as quiet influence, making small pauses, lowered expectations, and careful praise carry more weight than direct demands.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You forgot the concert. That's all right. I kept your ticket until the interval.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let me take you next week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's kind. I'll buy mine, and you can decide nearer the time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll buy both. Put it in my calendar now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Both tickets. How lovely. I'll put my name in the reminder too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely to hear from you, love. I took the phone to bed at nine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum, my shift ran late. I'll call at eight tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Eight would be lovely. I won't keep the evening clear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can promise ten minutes on my break.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ten minutes. That's thoughtful. I'll save the important things.

S102.editorialNote: A's careful understatement and withdrawn praise exert pressure without a direct command.

S103.title: When We Still Believed
S103.instruction: Use a shared earlier hope as your emotional home base, returning to it whenever the present feels uncertain or disappointing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This napkin still says we'll open a bookshop by the sea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We drew that before rent became real.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We also drew two chairs by the window. Could we put ours together tonight?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: In the flat? I need to work at that window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After work, then. I'll bring our books. Ten minutes pretending we're in our seaside bookshop before we look at the bills.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Remember when this jar was for our anniversary at the seaside?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We spent the money on the boiler.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We promised we'd swim together. The boiler didn't cancel that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's in three weeks. We can afford the bus to the reservoir.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put the bus fare in the jar. I'll pack the towels; we're still coming home with wet hair.

S103.editorialNote: A returns to an earlier shared hope as an emotional base without denying present disappointment.

S104.title: You Saw Me Through
S104.instruction: Treat past comfort you received as an enduring bond that should now earn honesty, patience, and reciprocal support.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You lent me this scarf when my marriage ended. Tell me honestly: should I answer his message?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't decide that for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You didn't decide anything that night. You stayed. Tell me what worries you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That you'll spend tonight waiting for another message.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then stay while I leave it unanswered. I'll make us tea this time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You sat with me when my shop closed. Will you help at the new stall? An honest answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know. My own shop's struggling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then forget the stall. You let me talk for hours when mine went.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we sit without talking first?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. You gave me three silent evenings. I've kept this one free.

S104.editorialNote: Past comfort creates an ongoing bond and a claim to honest reciprocal presence.

S105.title: The Strong One
S105.instruction: Be the strong one: steady everyone else, minimize your own needs, and resist any attempt to care for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've made everyone tea. I'll call Dad's friends about the funeral.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your hands are shaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it's good the calls don't require trays.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sit down. I'll call. Just give me their numbers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll dial for you. Peter will cry; I'll stay on the other phone in case you need rescuing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take the last tissue. Mum's funeral was hard on you. I've got my sleeve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're crying into both sleeves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They're washable. How's your daughter holding up?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's asleep. Come here. You can cry on my shoulder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You'll need that shoulder when she wakes. I'll get you a dry cardigan.

S105.editorialNote: A steadies others and rejects care directed toward their own visible need.

S106.title: Whose Pain Counts?
S106.instruction: Treat every disappointment as something to measure against what you have endured, competing for whose feelings deserve greater weight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One publisher turned you down? I've kept fourteen rejection letters.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you put them away? I came here for a hug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Though fourteen rejections ought to qualify me for more than one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come here. We can both have the same hug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then make it a long one. One rejection's worth for you, and thirteen more before you let go of me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've been unemployed a week. I've been out a year. This coffee should really be for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I bought it so you'd listen to what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll listen. Mine will take longer; there's twelve months to cover.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ten minutes each. I've got an interview.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An interview already? Then give me fifteen. You've started recovering.

S106.editorialNote: A measures another's disappointment against their own greater history and competes for conversational weight.

S107.title: My Safe Person
S107.instruction: Use one person’s reactions as your measure of safety, then downplay how much their reassurance changes you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay seated while I open this letter. Your face looks reassuring.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can open it without me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Keep looking like that while I prove it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know what's inside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You weren't supposed to let your face hear that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit beside me while I open the audition result. You've stopped smiling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm squinting at the screen. You haven't opened it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. So nothing's wrong. Move closer; the text is small.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm smiling now. Whatever it says, we'll get lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There. I can click it now. This chair was the problem.

S107.editorialNote: A uses one person's reaction as a safety gauge while denying dependence on that reassurance.

S108.title: Careful Around the Scar
S108.instruction: Treat one harmless detail as the trigger for an old hurt. Become overly careful, helpful, or controlled whenever it returns.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could we use any cups except the blue ones today?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happened with a blue cup?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nothing breakfast needs to revisit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put it away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Behind the plates, please. The handle's still looking this way.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you move that yellow envelope away from my birthday cake?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a voucher from your sister.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. My eviction notice came in yellow. I'll find her a nicer envelope.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the voucher out and bin this one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Under the coffee grounds, please. I'll hold the lid.

S108.editorialNote: A overcontrols one harmless cue associated with old hurt, keeping each scene on a single concrete trigger.

S109.title: Braver Than Me
S109.instruction: Treat another person’s emotional courage as both inspiring and unfair, resenting how exposed or hesitant it makes you feel.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You opened your rejection letter straight away. Must be nice, being brave on demand.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was scared too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You hid it very efficiently.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take your time with yours. I'll leave you alone to open it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, stay. I'm opening it now. You shouldn't get to be brave and considerate while I'm still finding the flap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You told them how you felt without rehearsing. I resent how impressive that was.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stumbled over half of it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even your stumbling looked courageous.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Want to practise with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Don't make practising look easy too.

S109.editorialNote: A admires emotional courage but resents how easily B appears to manage it.

S110.title: Before I Knew Better
S110.instruction: Perform the more hopeful version of yourself from before disappointment taught you caution, and defend that version when reality intrudes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've written when our shop opens. Before the first one failed, I never wrote if.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can't afford another empty opening party.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll bake. I used to assume people would come for my cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six portions. That's our budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Six generous portions. I'm writing 'come early' on the invitations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm entering the talent show. At seventeen I invited everyone before I'd even chosen a song.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you lost and wouldn't sing for a year.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm borrowing the version before that. Will you come?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Shall we sit at the back so you can slip out?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Front row, please. Seventeen-year-old me expected to spot her friends from the stage.

S110.editorialNote: A deliberately revives an older hopeful self and defends a hopeful statement against qualification.

S111.title: Waiting for the Bad News
S111.instruction: Treat pauses, changes, and uncertainty as signs that rejection or loss is approaching, then prepare yourself before it arrives.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You moved our meeting to Friday. I've brought a box for my desk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a promotion. You'll manage the new branch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Away from everyone? I'll pack before they have to say goodbye.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can still come to Friday drinks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll bring my own glass. Better get used to being a visitor before they stop inviting me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You paused when I asked about Saturday. Should I collect my things from your flat?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was swallowing tea. I'm taking you to dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Somewhere public. I'll bring tissues that fit in my sleeve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's at home. I'm cooking your favourite.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll bring containers. You shouldn't have my leftovers haunting the fridge afterwards.

S111.editorialNote: A prepares for loss before the uncertain message arrives and interprets reassurance as a possible preface.

S112.title: Let Me Carry It
S112.instruction: Take responsibility for managing everyone’s emotional burden, deciding what they should know, feel, and face.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the letter from the college. You've already had one disappointment today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum, it's my application.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And if it's another rejection, I'll tell you after you've eaten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can see 'Congratulations' through the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then after your brother's eaten. He didn't get in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take the condolence calls about Dad. You haven't slept.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want to speak to Aunt June.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll check whether she's crying before I put her through.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She wants me to comfort her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll comfort her first. You can have each other once I've got you both steady.

S112.editorialNote: A manages which emotional burdens others encounter, treating other people's autonomy as another burden to carry.

S113.title: Tell Me We’re Okay
S113.instruction: Treat every response as evidence of whether you are still accepted, and adjust yourself quickly whenever reassurance feels incomplete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Is my stool too close? I don't want you regretting our duet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're fine there. I need to see the music.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll move behind you. You won't have to look at me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I can't see you come in. Sit beside me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Beside you. Good. Could you nod before each entrance so I know you still want me joining in?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First dates don't need this many jokes. I'll stop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I liked the one about your dog.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just dog stories, then. I can do that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd like to hear about you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. I'll start with who I was before the dog. Too far back?

S113.editorialNote: Each incomplete reassurance triggers a practical adjustment intended to restore acceptance.

S114.title: Don’t Pity Me
S114.instruction: Frame your struggle as evidence of strength, steering concern toward admiration and rejecting anything that feels like pity.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You came to my solo show. Please stop saying 'brave' in that sad voice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Three people walked out. I wanted to buy you a drink.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I finished anyway. You can buy a drink for that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll invite the cast next door. They're celebrating a sellout.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Tell them I finished with no audience at all. Let's see them do that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I carried the entire move myself. Please stop making that poor-you face.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You must be exhausted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Impressively exhausted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I bring you tea?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. In the mug marked champion, not survivor.

S114.editorialNote: A redirects concern into respect for endurance, refusing the framing of pity.

S115.title: The Proper Way to Grieve
S115.instruction: Treat difficult feelings as requiring a precise ritual, sequence, or ceremony, and correct any attempt to rush or simplify it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we close the old café, one minute's silence for the kettle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was only a kettle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It worked here longer than either of us. Stand properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I unplug it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the minute. Don't interrupt its final shift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we hand over Mum's house keys, we say goodbye to her garden: roses, tree, shed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I tell the story about her locking us in the shed?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the tree. She planted that first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The buyers are waiting outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring them to the roses. If they're waiting for the keys, they can wait in the right order.
