S115.editorialNote: A controls an exact ritual of remembering or goodbye; the feeling is sincere and the comedy lies in procedure.

S116.title: Emotional Emergency
S116.instruction: Interpret every hesitation, sigh, or change in tone as the beginning of an emotional emergency requiring immediate intervention.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You sighed over dessert. I'll turn the music off so you can tell me what's wrong.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ate too much. That's all.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll clear it away. You don't need guilt sitting in front of you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please sit down. You're making me nervous.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nervous? I'm sitting. Shall I cancel our guests before this gets worse?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You hesitated before putting your veil on. Shall I send everyone out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The comb's caught in my hair. Help me untangle it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll free it. You shouldn't feel trapped on your wedding day.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just hurry. We're late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your voice changed. I'll tell Mum we need ten minutes with nobody expecting anything of you.

S116.editorialNote: A treats minor changes of expression as immediate emotional emergencies and escalates the intervention.

S117.title: Hope Is Evidence
S117.instruction: Treat every small kindness, coincidence, or improvement as undeniable proof that the best possible outcome is gathering momentum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The gallery thanked me for my paintings. Help me choose glasses for opening night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the automatic reply. Don't spend our rent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They're expecting enough interest to automate. We should buy in bulk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll lend you six glasses. That's all.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our first sponsor. I'll put your name on the invitations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've sold our first book. I'll extend the shop's opening hours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You bought it yourself. I'm refunding you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent service already. That brings people back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll buy one for my sister. Then we're closing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our first gift order. I'll stay overnight wrapping the rest; tomorrow we won't have time.

S117.editorialNote: A interprets tiny improvements as concrete evidence that the best outcome is already gathering momentum.

S118.title: What Do You Need Now?
S118.instruction: Accept every feeling as real, then translate it into water, space, a plan, a boundary, or the next practical step.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Opening night without the lead you wanted hurts. Water, or some space in my dressing room?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Water won't make me happy for her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. It just means you can be furious without a dry throat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's coming to ask if I'm okay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll ask her to wait until after the show. You only owe her your cues tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can be furious about the cancelled train and still have toast before we drive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't think about food.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll wrap it. You can decide when we're on the road.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Don't spend the drive telling me to calm down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. Directions only. The toast won't require a better attitude either.

S118.editorialNote: A validates the feeling without explanation and offers one concrete, negotiable practical support.

S119.title: That One Look
S119.instruction: Choose one small look, phrase, silence, or gesture and treat it as the clearest evidence of what everything truly means.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That half-wave outside tells me we're neighbours now, not friends.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I had shopping in both hands. Help me with this bag.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Groceries are still allowed across the boundary, then.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm making your birthday dinner. Come in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I will. But that wave says this is the last year you wanted to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You texted 'thanks.' for covering your shift. Are we just colleagues now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was rushing. You're my best man. Help me choose ties.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Plain black. That full stop makes this a formal appointment.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your speech is after dinner. Tell the story about our disastrous holiday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll list the dates and expenses. That full stop says we're past finding it funny.

S119.editorialNote: A treats one tiny signal as the definitive emotional evidence and examines it beyond B's explanation.

S120.title: A Turning Point
S120.instruction: Treat each emotional shift as proof that this moment will divide everything into before and after.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the first time we've laughed since the inheritance row. Write down today's date.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You tripped over Mum's footstool. I couldn't help it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I didn't mind. That's when we became sisters again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Good. Can we finally sort her furniture?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start a new list. That footstool reunited us; it doesn't go on the inventory from when we hated each other.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum, I said no to extra potatoes and didn't feel guilty. Put today's date on the calendar.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You left potatoes last Sunday too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That was fullness. This is independence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right. Serve your own gravy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My first unsupervised gravy. Pass me a clean plate; that one's from before.

S120.editorialNote: A declares an ordinary emotional shift to be the dividing point of life and formalises its aftermath.

D97.title: Let Me Lean
D97.instruction: Get someone to carry part of the emotional burden without making you name how heavy it has become.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you cancel our anniversary table? The restaurant number's on the fridge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What's happened?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please let the call be the first thing you take off me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call. They might ask whether you want another date.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say no for me. Then stay while I put the anniversary glasses away. You can tell me about your day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read the first line of this letter before I do.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Shall I read it aloud?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only if your face stays reasonably ordinary.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sit beside you. We can take one line at a time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep hold of the page too. I'll follow your finger. No need to ask why I'm taking so long.

D97.editorialNote: A asks for one concrete piece of support while avoiding an explanation of the whole emotional burden.

D98.title: Stay Until I’m Steady
D98.instruction: Keep someone present until you feel steady enough to face what comes next without them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay for tea. I need to tell the children about tomorrow's operation without crying.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've had three cups.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then skip the kettle. Let me practise telling you before I fetch them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My taxi's outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask for two minutes. Let me say 'I'll be in hospital' without apologising to you. Then I'll try telling them myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you leave me in the new flat, count five breaths with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was five. Shall I close the door?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not yet. Five more while I look at the empty kitchen instead of you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll wait here while you put the kettle on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay until it boils. Then I'll try pouring one cup without getting yours out.

D98.editorialNote: A delays separation until steadier, measuring the additional time in small concrete units.

D99.title: Understand the Hurt
D99.instruction: Make someone acknowledge why their action hurt, not merely agree that it happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I saved you a front-row seat at my concert. Do you understand why it hurt?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told you work might run late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I knew. I still looked at that empty seat before every song.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You needed someone there who knew what this meant to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. You'd heard me practise for months. Please tell me you understand why someone else couldn't fill it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I texted that I'd lost my job. You replied, 'What's for dinner?'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought something normal would help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Making your dinner? Can you see why I felt like the cook?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant we could go out. I'll book somewhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I believe you. Before you book, can you see why I heard a chore? I needed you to ask how I was.

D99.editorialNote: A asks B to understand the emotional meaning of a specific action rather than its practical cause.

D100.title: Tell Me I Did Enough
D100.instruction: Get someone to reassure you that your effort, choice, or survival was enough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I only finished one painting for our exhibition. Tell me I've done enough.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll spread mine out. Nobody will notice the gap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need to know I've contributed, not that you can hide where I haven't.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours belongs in the middle. It's the one people will see first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then introduce me as the other painter. No 'despite everything'. I want to hear that I belong here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I made it through the speech without leaving. Was that enough?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You forgot a paragraph.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. I'm asking about staying.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You stayed all the way through. I'll help you practise the missing bit tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could staying earn me tomorrow off? Tell me I can put the speech away.

D100.editorialNote: A seeks reassurance that a limited effort counts before being redirected to improvement.

D101.title: Start the Hard Part
D101.instruction: Get someone else to explain, announce, or begin the emotionally difficult part.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You tell the choir the tour's cancelled. I'll hand out the refund forms.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're the organiser.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. The forms will need my full attention.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They'll ask why.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say 'funding' first. I'll join after the disappointed silence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you phone Mum and begin the conversation about selling the house?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked to speak to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take over once you've said the word selling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put her on speaker. You'll be there for the whole thing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's fine. Introduce the idea, and when she says my full name, I'll answer.

D101.editorialNote: A gives someone else the emotionally difficult opening and volunteers for safe follow-up work.

D102.title: What Aren’t You Saying?
D102.instruction: Find out what someone is holding back by treating every careful answer as incomplete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You called my audition interesting. What came after that in your head?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're my sister. I'm trying to be encouraging.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me the encouraging half and the half you swallowed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your singing was better than your dancing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better by how much? Are we buying dance lessons or shoes that don't move?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: These minutes say 'discussion of my proposal.' What did you leave out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sign them and we can eat. Nobody wanted an awkward record.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: 'Nobody' sounds crowded. Who wanted my name out of it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I did. I suggested someone else present, to save your proposal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who else? You've recorded my rescue very carefully without naming my replacement.

D102.editorialNote: A treats careful phrasing as evidence of omitted material and narrows the gap B has left.

D103.title: Hope with Me
D103.instruction: Recruit someone into believing that the outcome can still change, even when the evidence is thin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Draw another route for our parade with me. Two streets said no; the town hasn't.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The only route left goes behind the supermarket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then take the other pencil. Can you picture people cheering by the loading bay?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My dad would come. He works there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put him on the map. Where would a second person stand?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Help me choose celebration glasses for when our café application gets approved.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're on the waiting list. I haven't even told my mum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then just believe it with me here. Which glasses belong in our café?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: These two. Mum would insist on a mug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Choose her mug too. You just pictured our first customer.

D103.editorialNote: A recruits active shared hope through a small concrete act rather than declaring optimism alone.

D104.title: Say the Scary Part
D104.instruction: Get someone else to name the frightening possibility or vulnerable feeling before you do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we open the landlord's letter, tell me the worst thing it could mean for our shop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've only missed one payment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know the number. I need you to say the thing I'm counting towards.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We could lose the shop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And what would that make me, after Dad trusted me with it? Say that bit first too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before our skating qualifier, can you say the possibility we keep avoiding?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want you carrying that onto the ice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm carrying it already. I just need you to say it first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We might not qualify. I'd still want to skate with you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why did I need that second sentence so much? Could you name that fear too?

D104.editorialNote: A seeks another voice to name the frightening possibility before naming it themselves.

D105.title: See What This Took
D105.instruction: Make someone recognize the courage, restraint, or emotional labor your choices required.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Compare the angry letter with the one I sent. Notice the crossing-out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I appreciate the apology you sent. Why show me the angry version?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because 'sorry' took ten minutes. Not sending the rest took all night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now I'm tempted to read what you spared me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please admire the thickness with it shut. I'd like one night's restraint to survive breakfast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I told the committee I couldn't chair another year. Please appreciate what those two sentences took.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Good. Could you stay on until we find someone?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I rehearsed in your car until I stopped apologising. That wasn't me advertising a temporary vacancy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll tell them you're exhausted and need a break.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please don't supply the excuse I spent an hour removing. Could you recognise a refusal I finally managed without one?

D105.editorialNote: A asks B to notice restraint or courage in the actual work, not just praise the final tidy result.

D106.title: Choose What Matters More
D106.instruction: Make someone choose between emotional safety and the outcome they claim to want.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They're calling your audition number. Do you want the part enough to let them hear you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want it. I don't want them laughing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can walk you in or drive you home. Which want am I helping?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Walk me in, but promise they won't laugh.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can promise I'll stay. Is that enough to risk the audition, or are we going home?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we renew this lease, do you want my honest answer about living together or a peaceful dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your honest answer. Just don't say anything that makes me panic.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can't promise both. Shall I answer, or shall we order?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Answer. But start by saying we're fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the answer you're choosing for me. Do you still want mine?

D106.editorialNote: A makes a conflict between safety and a desired result explicit, requiring a choice rather than both by default.

D107.title: Stay for the Hard Part
D107.instruction: Create increasing moments of emotional honesty to test whether someone remains present and supportive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I haven't booked our anniversary trip. Can you hear why before you get your laptop?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought you just needed help with the flights.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I let you think that. I was relieved when the cheap seats sold out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave the laptop shut. Is it the trip, or us?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Us. I hoped a cancellation would say it for me. Can you still sit beside me while I explain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wasn't just late to the reunion. Can I tell you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I saved you a seat beside me. Was it the traffic?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. I waited outside for half an hour. Can you hear why?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm here. But I thought you didn't want to sit with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wanted that seat. I was afraid you'd be happier without me there. Will you sit beside me now?

D107.editorialNote: A reveals progressively more difficult truth and uses continued presence as the test, without commanding B's response.

D108.title: Drop the Armor
D108.instruction: Persuade someone to lower their guard, stop performing strength, or admit what affects them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've locked the shop. You can stop doing the cheerful voice for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Someone has to keep morale up. You're my only employee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm off the clock. What did that empty till do to you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I cried in the stockroom. Then I practised smiling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You don't owe me a second performance. Can we lock the stockroom and let you be upset out here?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Over dinner you keep saying you're managing. What's hard about going home?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The silence. I leave the television on so it sounds occupied.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you ask me over instead of pretending you've got company?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cook. I promise I won't be miserable all evening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you invite me without that promise? I'd like to come even if you're miserable and we eat toast.

D108.editorialNote: A invites one manageable unguarded admission rather than demanding an emotional performance.

D109.title: I Started the Spiral
D109.instruction: Hide how much your own fear or resentment created the emotional crisis while helping everyone calm it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's reassure the stallholders that the fair is still on.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You panicked about the forecast and told them to cancel their vans.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I have the right contact list. I'll say the arrangements are unchanged.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Their arrangements changed because of you. Two vans are cancelled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll find replacements. Could your update call it a transport hiccup? They need something calm to read.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The club money's in the other envelope. Let's tell everyone they can stop worrying.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You phoned me crying that the treasurer had stolen it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you're the first person I'm reassuring. Could you pass on that it's all accounted for?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told the whole committee what you said.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll ring them together. Could you introduce it as a routine balance update? No need to replay the tears.

D109.editorialNote: A helps settle alarm that their own earlier fear created while diverting attention from its origin.

D110.title: Not the Real Fear
D110.instruction: Keep the conversation focused on practical details so no one reaches the fear underneath them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I open the scholarship letter, do we have clean teaspoons?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've made your tea. Open it; I want to know if you're leaving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put sugar in mine. I'll need another cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take mine. Are you frightened of going, or staying here with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If we swap cups, how will you know which has sugar? We need labels before anything gets mixed up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we discuss me moving out, can you check my train time again?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six twelve. I've checked five times, and your ticket's in your hand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Does this ticket work at the barrier, or do I need the booking email?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll walk you through the barrier. Are you scared of leaving me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If you're coming onto the platform, we need to check whether you need a ticket too.

D110.editorialNote: A stays in concrete practical details to avoid exposing the fear underneath.

D111.title: Let Them Keep Hope
D111.instruction: Hide discouraging information because you believe hope is the only thing keeping someone able to continue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's pack your paintings for the last gallery. You've finally picked up a brush again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: If the big gallery rejected me too, I'm done. Did they write?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Their letter can wait. This gallery still needs your best three.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Pick them, then. I can't face another envelope.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll handle the envelopes. You finish the blue one; there's still somewhere for it to go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the seed packets. The allotment letter says we're on the waiting list.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've covered our number. If it's another year indoors, I'm giving up gardening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The important bit is we're on it. Let's start tomatoes on my windowsill.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'll get tired of them before we get a plot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my sunny room. I'll move the bed; keep the packets.

D111.editorialNote: A hides discouraging evidence to preserve another person's ability to continue hoping.

D112.title: Admit You’re Hurt
D112.instruction: Get someone to admit hurt, fear, or disappointment before you reveal that you feel it too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When Mum cancelled our birthday dinner, were you disappointed?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Were you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like your answer before I give mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I cried in the supermarket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Me too. I told the cashier the birthday candles were seasonal allergies.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did the boss calling us office furniture hurt you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why? Are you making a complaint?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's still in drafts. How did you feel?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Invisible. I've worked here twelve years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Me too. Mine says 'unprofessional'; I'm changing that to 'I went home and cried.'

D112.editorialNote: A asks B to admit hurt first while concealing their own matching distress.

D113.title: A Necessary Heartbreak
D113.instruction: Describe disappointment, rejection, or loss as the exact experience everyone needed in order to grow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That rejection was exactly the lesson our bakery needed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We needed the contract.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And now we've learned not to need one contract.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can't pay the mixer loan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A powerful second lesson about attachment to equipment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm sorry I broke your graduation mug. Losing it is exactly how we learn to let go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want to glue it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That urge is why we needed this. We've confused a degree with a drinking vessel.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then give me your graduation mug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Losing mine will teach me generosity. We should both drink from jam jars tomorrow.

D113.editorialNote: A turns disappointment into an allegedly necessary growth experience, even as B wants the lost outcome back.

D114.title: I Can Handle This
D114.instruction: Perform complete emotional readiness while quietly borrowing coping strategies from every response around you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm ready for our audition results. Why are you breathing like that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Four in, six out. It stops my hands shaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Four in, six out. I like to arrive already regulated.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I also write down who I'll call if I don't get in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. Lend me your pen; my support network deserves advance notice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm completely prepared for this rejection email. Why have you brought water?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Small sips helped when I lost my job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My approach exactly. Leave the jug; I prefer a thorough preparation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I had my sister read the email aloud. Want me to?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. I always arrange a reader. Start gently; that's part of my system.

D114.editorialNote: A borrows practical coping strategies while claiming they were already part of their own method.

D115.title: Outfeel the Room
D115.instruction: Answer every fear, sacrifice, or disappointment with one of your own that deserves more attention.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One sleepless night before your interview? I've been awake all week worrying about mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I just need you to practise questions with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask why I left my last job. You'll understand why my interview is harder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm scared I'll freeze.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm scared I'll cry. Let's use your practice time to get me through the greeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your opening had empty seats? Mine had two people, and both left.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry. Have my complimentary drink.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. My theatre couldn't even afford to console us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you listen now? My dad left before my scene.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mine asked for a refund. Could you stay while I finish this? I haven't told anyone that.

D115.editorialNote: Each emotional disclosure becomes an opening for A's larger competing experience.

D116.title: Hope Keeps Moving
D116.instruction: Turn every disappointment into a new reason the desired outcome is delayed, redirected, or becoming more meaningful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The hall rejected our wedding booking. Apparently we're meant to marry somewhere less municipal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Every venue is booked for June.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then September gives us three more months to practise being married.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My parents can't travel in September.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we go to them. Their garden! We're finally finding out where this wedding belongs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our bookshop failed here. We're meant to find readers somewhere else.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We have no moving money.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we're meant to start smaller. One shelf, properly chosen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I could get us a market stall beside the bus stop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: People waiting with nothing to read! I'll pack the short stories. We've been making our customers come too far.

D116.editorialNote: A redirects hope after each specific failure while insisting the desired outcome remains in motion.

D117.title: Comfort Everyone Else
D117.instruction: Meet every painful moment by comforting someone else more intensely while your own distress becomes harder to hide.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've brought tissues. Being laid off together doesn't make your day any easier.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're wiping your eyes on your sleeve.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm saving the soft ones for you. Tell me what you're worried about.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You. You can't even get the tissue box open.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then take the whole box. I'll make tea once my hands stop doing this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've made you soup. The choir rejecting us doesn't mean you should miss dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've set a bowl for yourself too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So you won't have to eat alone. I'll butter your bread.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sit with me. I don't want you crying in the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right. But take my bread too. I can't swallow yet, and you shouldn't have to ask twice.

D117.editorialNote: A intensifies care for B to prevent attention returning to A's visible distress.

D118.title: Emotional Interest
D118.instruction: Treat comfort, vulnerability, and forgiveness as investments that must eventually be repaid with equal emotional risk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I told your mother I'm scared she dislikes me. Sunday, you owe me an equally embarrassing admission.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't ask you to tell her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I trusted you to risk something too. What scares you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That she'll like you more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's equal. Now tell her over lunch. Mine had an audience; yours needs one too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll stay through this hard conversation. Someday I need you equally open with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you keeping score?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not points. A place where both of us can be unsteady.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know if I can.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then say that honestly. It's a first payment.

D118.editorialNote: A treats vulnerability as a reciprocal emotional investment, asking B for equivalent exposure.

D119.title: Ready on My Terms
D119.instruction: Agree to be honest, hopeful, or vulnerable only in forms that preserve your emotional safety.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll talk about last night's rent argument, but not the whole year tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole year matters. You've been pulling away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It does. One question, and let me finish before you answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right. Were you going to move out?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I packed a bag. It's still upstairs. Please let that be the whole answer for a minute.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll sit by the door while we talk about trying again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you planning to run?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Knowing I can leave is helping me stay.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can stop when you need to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I want to come home. Please don't hand me a key yet; saying it is enough for tonight.

D119.editorialNote: A agrees to vulnerability within an explicit boundary that makes participation possible.

D120.title: The Same Ending
D120.instruction: Use every new emotional detail as evidence that the same feared ending is becoming inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You ended your message with 'take care.' That's how my last breakup started.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said you had a cold. I meant get better.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He wanted me healthy before he left too. Less guilt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll bring you soup tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So we're at the final kindness. Will it be in a container you don't need back?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First you cancel lunch, then stop calling, then ask for the key.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've only cancelled lunch. I'm exhausted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what he said before seeing me became another job.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tomorrow, then? I'll book our usual table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He chose a restaurant too. Public enough that I couldn't beg. Book the corner, please.

D120.editorialNote: New details are interpreted as steps toward the same feared ending, not merely general anxiety.

S121.title: The Keeper of Secrets
S121.instruction: Carry yourself as the person entrusted with what others cannot know, letting selective disclosure determine what everyone is allowed to discuss.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The organiser left me the picnic briefing. You can tell the drivers the departure time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They need the destination for their satnavs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send them to me individually. I'll disclose one postcode per driver.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're all sharing one minibus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then nominate one driver. I'll tell him outside. The others can discuss the departure time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bride left me these envelopes. You can announce the tables, but not who's sitting together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm seating the guests. They need names.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me one guest at a time. I'll release their chair.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I at least take couples together?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me which couple. I'll disclose whether they're still being seated as one.

S121.editorialNote: A determines the permitted subject matter through staged disclosure rather than simply keeping everything secret.

S122.title: Authority by Bluff
S122.instruction: Project control through confident half-answers while guarding the possibility that one direct question could expose how little you actually know.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've got tomorrow's inspection covered. Leave the folder with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Does page four say we need two sinks?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It requires an appropriate number for the operation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The plumber's here. Shall I ask him to read it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Have him quote for one and two. I'll confirm which interpretation we're implementing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know why the shop alarm sounded. We can open on time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Was it the back door or the motion sensor?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The system detected activity in the relevant area.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll bring up the log. You can show me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read me your interpretation first. I don't want my findings influencing yours.

S122.editorialNote: Confident half-answers conceal A's lack of knowledge until a precise question threatens the bluff.

S123.title: Professional Suspicion
S123.instruction: Treat inconsistencies, evasions, and missing details as evidence your trained eye should investigate before anyone proceeds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I approve your expenses: the receipt says four, your note says four-oh-five.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I bought a biscuit on the way back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then there's a second transaction missing from your account.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I paid for it myself. Here, have the other one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two biscuits. I'll need to revise the timeline before I sign.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we hand over the shop keys, why did you cross out cupboard and write shelf?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cleaner moved them onto the shelf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When? I need the last confirmed sighting before we sign.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nine. I saw them there. She doesn't start until ten.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then who moved them before she arrived? Get her on the phone; we now need two accounts of one shelf.

S123.editorialNote: A treats small inconsistencies as investigative evidence and follows a specific discrepancy through B's practical explanation.

S124.title: Cleared to Know
S124.instruction: Treat access to private information as proof that you belong, and exclusion from any detail as a challenge to your legitimacy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pass me the unredacted reunion plan. I'm family, not the public.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That page lists everyone's surprise presents.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Family should get more than the visitor edition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It includes your present.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell me who chose it. I should know who considers me family.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why does my club briefing have blacked-out names?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only the organising committee sees those.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I stacked every chair for that committee. Surely I've earned the names.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can apply next month. I'll sponsor you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Could you put one name in my copy now, so I know you're sponsoring a member?

S124.editorialNote: Restricted information becomes a test of A's membership; B's practical boundary triggers a more personal demand.

S125.title: The Initiated One
S125.instruction: Treat others as recent initiates, revealing rules and information in carefully measured doses that preserve your seniority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your first shift on the club door. I'll teach you half the secret handshake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Don't I need the whole thing to admit people?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can greet them. I'll handle admission until you've progressed to the wrist.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The president wants me to train tomorrow's doorman.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Teach him the fingers. I'll teach you the wrist while he waits outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Welcome to the club. Tonight I'll teach you rule one: discretion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The secretary gave me the whole rulebook.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Keep it closed while we establish discretion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked me to proofread it before printing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then read me each sentence. I'll tell you which ones you're ready to understand.

S125.editorialNote: A dispenses knowledge as initiation and preserves rank by withholding the next step.

S126.title: Information Is Leverage
S126.instruction: Remain outwardly cooperative while controlling one useful fact, releasing only enough of it to shape each decision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can help find your parcel. The van number starts with four; let's check my route first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are six vans starting with four.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only two end in seven. Mine passes both.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine, your route. Which van do we stop at?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Happy to guide you. Take my overdue collection first, then I'll point it out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can trace your missing projector approval. It came from upstairs; shall we review my repair budget together?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Was it the director or her deputy?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The signature starts with M. Let's put repairs on today's agenda.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're on. Purchasing still needs the surname.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Move repairs before refreshments and I'll give you the name for the purchase order.

S126.editorialNote: A releases useful information incrementally to shape decisions while sounding cooperative.

S127.title: Our First Secret
S127.instruction: Treat a shared secret from the beginning of the relationship as the truest proof of what still connects you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit with me at the reunion. We became friends hiding the headmaster's bicycle behind that purple gate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the headmaster now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're still the only headmaster who knows where we'd hide it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll save you a seat, but I have to give the welcome speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then begin with 'purple gate.' Everyone else will hear a welcome; I'll know you're still talking to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we pack Mum's biscuit tin, knock twice. That was our first secret.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She knew we emptied it. She told me years ago.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You still kept our signal. There's my brother.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You take the tin. We hardly see each other now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then knock twice when you visit. I'll know you're here for our tin, even if it's full.

S127.editorialNote: An old shared secret is treated as the durable core of connection, even when its practical relevance has vanished.

S128.title: I Covered for You
S128.instruction: Carry past concealment as an unpaid favor, expecting trust, access, and protection whenever the old debt becomes relevant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I told Dad you were with me when you dented his car. Tell him I didn't break his greenhouse.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was ten years ago.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ten years I've kept your evening accounted for. I need one afternoon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I won't lie. I'll come with you while you tell him.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sit beside me. If he calls me careless, remind him how reliable I've been for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Show me next month's private rota. I told the manager you were making deliveries when you missed that shift.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thanked you. I can't give you the manager's password.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You trusted me with a whole missing afternoon. I only want to see Saturdays.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll check your Saturdays myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And put us together. If anyone questions it, say I'm someone you can rely on.

S128.editorialNote: A treats an old cover story as an unpaid investment requiring current loyalty or protection.

S129.title: The Cleanup Person
S129.instruction: Return to the familiar role of containing damage, correcting stories, and protecting everyone from the consequences of disclosure.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you explain the broken window to Mum, give me your versions. Like last time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said football. Jamie said the wind.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we start with the broken window and our offer to pay. Leave weather out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Jamie already texted her about a storm.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the repair quote. I'll send something useful before she asks which storm plays football.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've peeled the surprise-party labels off the boxes by her desk. Same rescue service as last year.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thank you. I told her they're printer supplies.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll move the balloons before she asks which printer takes helium.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She offered to unpack them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell her I'll handle it. She already thinks I do all the office jobs; we can keep the cake under that.

S129.editorialNote: A reflexively repairs stories and evidence for others, treating contradictory details as a familiar cleanup job.

S130.title: First to Solve It
S130.instruction: Treat each clue and inconsistency as a contest over who can understand the situation first and most completely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've solved your missing parcel. Tracking says reception; you were still refreshing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Reception signed for three boxes. Only two reached our office.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then one stayed downstairs. I've narrowed your whole building to one desk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The trolley's here. There's a box wedged underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So it left reception but never got unloaded. You've found the parcel; I've solved why we've been calling reception all morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our mystery judge is the baker. Flour on the invitation. Solved before you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The miller uses flour too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it's the miller. I've already moved past the obvious answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on the envelope flap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The baker, licking it after decorating. I've got the identity and the sequence; you've got ingredients.

S130.editorialNote: A competes over discovery itself; each collaborative step becomes a claim to having solved first.

S131.title: Only You Can Know
S131.instruction: Treat one person as the only safe place for your honest reactions, while hiding how much their discretion determines what you can risk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Close the office door. I hated the director's presentation. You're the only person I can say that to.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He asked me to collect feedback.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me down as engaged. This is just us having coffee.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave your comments out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thanks. The standing ovation felt like a hostage video. More coffee?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're the only one who's read my notebook. I don't want to take over Dad's shop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He wants me to bring it to Sunday lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring the accounts notebook. This one's mostly spelling mistakes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll keep this one here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could I add something? I was relieved when the freezer broke. Terrible spelling on that page.

S131.editorialNote: A reserves honest speech for one trusted person and downplays how much their discretion enables it.

S132.title: The Missing Truth
S132.instruction: Treat every present exchange as incomplete until an old concealment, unanswered question, or broken confidence is finally addressed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we book our anniversary trip, why did you leave Venice early?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll stay the whole week this time. Nonrefundable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You paid for the last night then, too. What happened?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum was ill. She asked me not to tell anyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You could have said that afterwards. When you said you needed space from me, was that her request too?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll renew my club membership once you explain why my curtain vote vanished.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're voting on curtains again. You can choose first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Where will you put my choice this time? Last year's blue never reached the minutes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll make you minute secretary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then my first entry is 'Previous vote still unaccounted for.' Who can answer that?

S132.editorialNote: An old unanswered question interrupts current practical business until its missing truth is acknowledged.

S133.title: Envious of the Lie
S133.instruction: Treat another person’s composure under scrutiny as both impressive and unfair, resenting how easily they seem to control what others believe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You told the manager you hadn't lost the keys and he believed you instantly. How do you do that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I hadn't lost them. I need you to tell him that too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: With my face? You get innocence; I get follow-up questions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll stand beside you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. Could you look impressed when I tell the truth? Yours carries more weight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your hands stayed still when the treasurer asked about the missing cash. Mine made me look guilty.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put them in your pockets. We both need to finish these statements.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You get believed naturally. I need special trousers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here, hold my statement. That'll keep them busy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even your paper looks innocent. Can mine go underneath it?

S133.editorialNote: A admires apparent innocence and copies its delivery while resenting their own visible strain.

S134.title: Before We Knew
S134.instruction: Return emotionally to the time before a difficult truth changed what you could believe, trust, or say openly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you take Dad's fake trophy out of the cabinet, can I look at our photo?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You look so proud of him in it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That was a lovely person to be. I thought he'd beaten twelve cyclists.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can keep the photo without displaying the trophy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could we put it by my bike? I started riding that afternoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could the club's victory bunting stay up until tea? I liked us before we knew about the altered scores.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The visiting team arrives in ten minutes. We owe them the trophy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. I just remember hanging this with you. We hugged on a stepladder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll hold it while you take the bunting down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you hug me first? Same ladder. Less to celebrate.

S134.editorialNote: A seeks a moment in the old explanation before accepting a new difficult truth, without disputing the evidence.

S135.title: Everyone Knows Something
S135.instruction: Interpret private conversations, careful wording, and unexplained pauses as signs that important information is being kept from you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why did everyone stop talking when I came into the staff kitchen?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We'd finished choosing lunch. Do you want noodles?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Is noodles what you're calling the thing I'm not supposed to know?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Look, here's the order. Yours is already on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You decided what I'd want before I arrived. How long have you been discussing me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Both notebooks closed when I sat down for the rota meeting. Am I being replaced?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine has my medical appointments in it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And does Jen keep your appointments too, or did you agree on that explanation?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ask Jen about hers. You aren't reading mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So she's handling questions and you're guarding the records. When was that decided?

S135.editorialNote: Ordinary privacy is interpreted as evidence of exclusion, with each denial becoming another suspicious detail.

S136.title: Protection Through Silence
S136.instruction: Protect others by withholding details, redirecting questions, and managing timing because you trust your own judgment about when the truth should surface.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll give you the landlord's letter once you're sitting down. You've only just got home.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's addressed to me. Is he selling our flat?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's get you out of this doorway before we discuss where we'll live.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sitting. Give it here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's your favourite chair. Come to the kitchen; I'd rather you didn't remember this whenever you sit there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll give you the last page of the review after your concert.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Does it say anything about my voice?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It says things you don't need to carry onto a stage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then give it to me in the interval.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's before your solo. I'll bring you water in the interval. Water hasn't formed an opinion.

S136.editorialNote: A withholds information based on their own assessment of another person's readiness and timing.

S137.title: Trusted with This
S137.instruction: Treat being confided in as proof of closeness, and guard that privileged role whenever information begins spreading.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You told me about the move before your family. I thought that meant we were especially close.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We are. I'm telling them tonight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you call me just before? One last conversation where it's ours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come to dinner. You can help me tell them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you say I already knew? I want to sit beside you, not among the surprised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why is there another chair? I thought only I knew you were selling the bakery.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam's buying it. He needs to see the accounts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. You told me because we're close; he's getting spreadsheets.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He'll need to know why I'm selling, too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you tell me how you feel about telling him before he arrives? That part could still be ours.

S137.editorialNote: Being the original confidant is treated as proof of closeness; wider disclosure threatens that special role.

S138.title: I Figured It Out
S138.instruction: Create opportunities to reveal that you noticed the pattern first while pretending recognition matters less than solving the problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you brief the volunteers, every escaped rabbit used the east gate. I spotted that Tuesday, if a timeline helps.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were right. I'll tell them to check that latch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mention Tuesday so they understand how long this was preventable.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then come explain the check yourself. I need to catch the rabbits.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Could you introduce me as the person who spotted it? Saves explanation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my Tuesday note beside the leaking freezer. It identifies the overnight power cuts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Good. The engineer needs the times, not our names.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My initials distinguish observed times from later guesses. Purely useful.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then write the repair request yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. 'Following my Tuesday discovery' gets the chronology settled before we trouble him with temperatures.

S138.editorialNote: A engineers recognition for early insight while pretending the timing is merely factual accuracy.

S139.title: The Secrecy Protocol
S139.instruction: Treat concealment as a precise ritual with passwords, signals, approved phrases, and severe consequences for careless improvisation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Write the password before I hand over the surprise picnic sandwiches.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're alone in the kitchen, and the bus leaves in two minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then write quickly. Speaking it cancels collection.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've written cucumber. That's yesterday's password, isn't it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've said it. The sandwiches stay here. I'll tell the walkers their lunch failed clearance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Signal Mum's birthday cake location: three fingers for cupboard, four for fridge. Say it aloud and you're off the surprise team.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's on the table. The helpers need to find it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're off. Table is a flat palm. I'll signal them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already sent them a photo. That doesn't say anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It shows everything. Now we move the cake and change the signals. You won't be told where your slice is.

S139.editorialNote: Secrecy is an exact ritual even for trivial business; B's convenience request creates another protocol requirement.

S140.title: The Leak Is Spreading
S140.instruction: Interpret every new question or coincidence as evidence that concealed information is escaping faster than it can be contained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The florist asked what time our surprise party starts. How did it get out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told her so she'd deliver before Dad arrives.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now the driver knows. Can you collect the flowers yourself?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I'll ask the baker to give me a lift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's reached the baker while we were containing the florist. How many stops is this lift making?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why are there three copies of our private resignation letter on your desk?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One for each of us and a spare. Nobody else has seen it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The spare is a conversation waiting to happen. Shred it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I use the accounts shredder? Ours is jammed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Accounts already? We haven't destroyed one copy and it's reached another department. Who there knows?

S140.editorialNote: A interprets every extra question or copy as accelerating escape of information and expands containment.

S141.title: A Delicious Mystery
S141.instruction: Treat every missing fact, contradiction, and suspicious detail as delightful proof that the situation is becoming more interesting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The budget page is missing from our club minutes. Someone's made accounts night interesting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The treasurer took it home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. A suspect with homework. Shall we ring her?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's here. She says she never took it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A contradiction in person! Bring her a chair beside mine; I'm staying for the whole meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You ordered our anniversary cake, but the baker says we cancelled. What an intriguing start.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have the receipt. It says collected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cancelled and collected! Let's ask who collected it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He says you did. He has your signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And now I'm involved! Bring the receipt; this is much more personal than dinner.

S141.editorialNote: Missing or contradictory facts delight A and create further investigative appetite.

S142.title: Cover Story Logistics
S142.instruction: Accept that a secret plan exists, then focus on schedules, witnesses, explanations, cleanup, and what everyone must remember.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For Dad's surprise picnic, where can forty guests board the bus unseen?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Outside my shop. Dad never goes there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Tell everyone to arrive separately so the neighbours don't mention a crowd.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Dad's offered to open the shop for me while I organise it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then board at the library. Ring all forty guests; no group message Dad might see. Who's collecting him after we leave?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For Mum's surprise party, we're saying you brought the cake on the nine o'clock bus?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. She'll ask why she didn't see my car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The last bus leaves at eight. Can you claim you walked?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She drove past me at half eight. I was empty-handed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the cake was already here. We need Dad to remember accepting it before his nap.

S142.editorialNote: A accepts secrecy and tests its concrete logistics, witnesses and timing.

S143.title: One Suspicious Detail
S143.instruction: Choose one ordinary detail and treat it as the clue that will expose the entire hidden story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The painting's gone. That red thread on its frame will explain everything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My scarf caught there last night. Can we open the gallery?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This thread will date the theft. Was the painting there then?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. But I picked that thread off before leaving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then this one means someone came back wearing your scarf. Keep it on; we'll reconstruct the whole night from this snag.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This coffee ring is the key to the missing keys.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The keys are in your pocket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then explain why the cup was beside them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You put it there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And now we have the movement sequence.

S143.editorialNote: One specific mundane clue dominates A's explanation while larger evidence is held back.

S144.title: Competing Theories
S144.instruction: Create several explanations for what is happening. Test each new clue against them, and switch allegiance whenever one theory gains strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our wedding cake's gone: theft, accident, or the dog. I suspect theft.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on him. Get him outside before Mum sees.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dog leads. I'll take him; check under the table for crumbs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That icing's from yesterday. The crumbs lead into the cloakroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Theft leads again. Keep the dog here; let's see whether that trail ends at a dropped cake or somebody's coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The hall lights failed: weather, wiring, or the caretaker saving electricity. Wiring's my favourite.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He unplugged them. Help me reach the socket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Economy takes the lead. I'll hold your ladder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The socket's wet. There's rain coming through the roof.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Weather overtakes him. Leave the plug; let's ask whether he unplugged it before the leak.

S144.editorialNote: A maintains competing explanations and changes allegiance as real clues favor one over another.

D121.title: Help Me Keep This Quiet
D121.instruction: Get someone to help contain a secret without first revealing its full risk or purpose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hide this envelope under the picnic hamper before Mum comes in.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked me to unpack the hamper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then keep the envelope in your pocket while you unpack.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll end up taking it home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. I'll explain when she stops asking where it is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the spare cupboard key till tomorrow. Don't tell your flatmate I've left it here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you tell me what's in the cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you accept knowing what isn't? Nothing alive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you collect it before she gets home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. Text me when she leaves work. Just 'key', please.

D121.editorialNote: A asks for help containing one concrete secret before explaining its stakes.

D122.title: Not Until You Explain
D122.instruction: Keep someone present until they account for one contradiction, omission, or suspicious change in their story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you catch that bus: you said work kept you till six. Why's your taxi receipt timed five?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll explain tomorrow. That's the last bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll drive you. What happened to that hour?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I left at five. I stopped somewhere before I came home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll drive you home after you tell me where you stopped. Sit down; I've got all evening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wait before you go. You said our wedding venue was booked for Friday. This says Monday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Monday was cheaper. Can you sign? I'm late for work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay while I read it. You told me Friday was confirmed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was. I moved it after we sent the invitations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then work needs to wait. Explain when you planned to tell the Friday guests.

D122.editorialNote: A uses a precise contradiction to hold B in the conversation until it is accounted for.

D123.title: Apologize for the Lie
D123.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that the concealment or misdirection mattered, even if the underlying choice was defensible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm not asking you to apologise for cancelling. Apologise for not telling me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't want to upset you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So you let me arrive with a cake instead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry the party didn't happen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Try the part where I didn't know.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You showed me the rescue dog's photo, not the page saying he eats sofas.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He needed a home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I understand. Admit that hiding the sofa page changed my yes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll buy you another sofa.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Before we feed him another one, say I should have had both pages.

D123.editorialNote: A distinguishes the concealed information from the underlying decision and asks for acknowledgment of that harm.

D124.title: Approve the Cover Story
D124.instruction: Get someone to endorse an explanation that protects the plan, reputation, or people involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you back 'collecting chairs' when the caretaker asks why we opened the props cupboard? We need him to lend us the hall again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Chairs don't fit in there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Checking for folding stools, then. Can you back that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you admit you borrowed his key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Borrowed his key to check for extra seating. Will you sign the hall request with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can you approve 'delivery delay' in the newsletter? I don't want our new volunteer blamed for the melted cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She delivered it on time. We left it by the radiator.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then 'storage problem'. Will you approve that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if we mention the refund.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. 'Storage problem; full refund arranged.' Can I put your name under it?

D124.editorialNote: A seeks agreement on a protective shared explanation and negotiates emphasis around contradictory facts.

D125.title: You Handle the Evidence
D125.instruction: Make someone else take responsibility for the evidence, loose end, or difficult follow-up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the raffle cashbox in your office till the treasurer comes. I can't face explaining the broken lock.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My office doesn't lock either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then take it home. You can hand it to her tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll want me to count it with her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. You handle the count and explain the lock; I'll send you the key that snapped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you explain my missing magician's receipt to the treasurer? You booked him.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You paid him. I only found his number.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then ring him for a replacement. You've got the number.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He won't send a duplicate unless the treasurer emails him directly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then draft her email and get her to send it. Copy yourself in so you can chase him.

D125.editorialNote: A hands evidence or follow-up to someone else, using their own visible involvement as the reason to delegate.

D126.title: What Really Happened?
D126.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For this missing-parcel form: was it a bag or a box? You've said both.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A bag, I think. I carried it by the handles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Describe the handles. Were they attached to fabric or cardboard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Cardboard. It had a rigid lid, too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why 'bag'? Tell me again what you carried. Was the box inside something?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're claiming for your lost bag. At four, were you on the bus or buying coffee? You've told me both.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Coffee. Can we finish the form?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was the bag beside you when you paid?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. The driver waited while I ran in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So both fit. Tell me the boarding bit again: did the bag come back out with you?

D126.editorialNote: A compares concrete details across repeated accounts and tests consistency instead of assuming guilt.

D127.title: Back My Version
D127.instruction: Recruit someone to remember, repeat, and defend one shared version of events when questions begin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The allotment committee's asking about the greenhouse. We arrived after the glass broke, remember?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I saw your wheelbarrow hit it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We came inside afterwards. Can we both tell them we were clearing up?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll say that. I won't lie about the wheelbarrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then start with clearing up. If they ask about the barrow, we moved it away afterwards. Let's both use that order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The caretaker's asking about our extra key. Tell him we were checking the cake cupboard's lock.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We did check it. Then we ate the cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with the part we both remember as maintenance.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He'll ask why there are crumbs in the lock.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we both remember a blockage. Say that back so we're consistent.

D127.editorialNote: A recruits a rehearsed shared account and revises the delivery when B's memory conflicts.

D128.title: Test the Story First
D128.instruction: Get someone else to repeat the explanation, ask the dangerous question, or test the risky step before you commit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Try this banking-delay explanation for the missing raffle money on the chair before I sign it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not defending your accounts again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just test the explanation. If she accepts it, I'll sign and handle every question.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll recognise your handwriting before I speak.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the paper. Ask whether a banking delay sounds plausible. If she asks whose money, come back before answering.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask Dad why our holiday account's empty. I'll wait by the kitchen door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come with me. You booked the flights.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask whether he's angry about the price first. If he isn't, I'll come in.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask, but I'm calling you in if he wants the flight receipt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask whether he wants the total or the breakdown before you call me. The seat upgrades need a longer explanation.

D128.editorialNote: A has someone else test an explanation or dangerous question before deciding how publicly to commit.

D129.title: Credit for the Discovery
D129.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that you found the clue, saw through the deception, or designed the successful scheme.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before calling it our discovery, mention who found the receipt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We all solved the problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. After my receipt introduced it properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put your name in the report.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Beside found, not beside attended.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: On tomorrow's house tour, will you say my diagram revealed the hidden doorway?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum spent all week stripping that wall.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Credit her work. Then say who spotted the door before we stripped it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll let you open it for the visitors.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Introduce me as the person who found it, or they'll think I'm holding it for them.

D129.editorialNote: A seeks explicit credit for the first clue or design before group ownership erases the contribution.

D130.title: Truth or Loyalty
D130.instruction: Make someone choose between protecting the relationship and answering a dangerous question honestly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum's asking who broke her vase. Will you tell her, or keep your promise to your little brother?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's blaming the cleaner. I can't let that happen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Clear the cleaner. Do you have to name me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's asked me directly whether you did it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then are you answering her, or keeping the promise I trusted you with?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The client asked who wrote our pitch. Will you tell her I copied it, or protect our partnership?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can withdraw it together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll withdraw it. Will you keep my name out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked whether you copied it. Withdrawing doesn't answer her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then before you say yes, decide whether we're still partners when she puts down the phone.

D130.editorialNote: A forces an explicit tradeoff between honest disclosure and protecting an existing confidence.

D131.title: Can You Keep It?
D131.instruction: Use increasingly sensitive details to test whether someone deserves deeper trust.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The club's changing the menu. Keep that quiet before I tell you the bigger news.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I won't tell anyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not even the person you tell everything to?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You mean Sam?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. We've found the first lock to check.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I withdrew my college application. Have you told Mum?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked. I said my sister's plans were hers to explain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then there's more. I've leased a bakery. Can I send you the address?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Call me. Mum uses my tablet; she'd see the message.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good catch. I'll call. It's Mum's old bakery. I want you there when I tell her.

D131.editorialNote: A offers graduated disclosures and tests where B would take each one, rather than demanding instant trust.

D132.title: Hand Over the Proof
D132.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender information, evidence, a key, or access that would let you proceed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the actual note, not your description.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can read it to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I want the words that don't get your emphasis.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's private.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then show me the one line you're using to decide for me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand me the drawer key before I sign the club accounts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll tell you the total.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My signature covers the receipts too. Let me check how it adds up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: If you find a mistake, my name goes on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put mine beside yours. Give me the key and we'll correct it together before either name goes outside this room.

D132.editorialNote: A pursues the original evidence rather than accepting B's summary or control over access.

D133.title: Steer the Suspicion
D133.instruction: Hide your responsibility by redirecting every new clue toward a safer explanation before anyone can connect it back to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That ink on your new sofa must be from the delivery label.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The label's dry. You signed with your fountain pen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the driver brushed my signature against the fabric. We should photograph it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your pen's still leaking onto the cushion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The delivery must have cracked it when they squeezed past me. Photograph the pen too; that's a second claim.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your shelf fell because they supplied the wrong bracket.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You fitted it upside down. Look at the arrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a misleading arrow. We should photograph it for the manufacturer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You drew that arrow. I watched you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because theirs was missing. Put that in the complaint; they made us supply our own safety markings.

D133.editorialNote: A redirects evidence of their responsibility to a plausible safer cause; each clue changes the diversion.

D134.title: Anything but That Question
D134.instruction: Redirect every attempt to discuss the one detail that could expose your real motive or involvement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll return your spare key after dinner. Have you booked somewhere?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I never gave you a spare key. Where did you get it?

beats.speaker: A
